nodes.title: Transformation law of eta quotients on Γ₀(N)
nodes.statement: Let r : ℕ →₀ ℤ with every δ ∈ supp r positive and dividing N, k = (1/2)Σ r_δ. For γ = (a b; c d) ∈ Γ₀(N) and τ ∈ ℍ: η_r(γτ) = v_r(γ)·((cτ + d)^{1/2})^{2k}·η_r(τ) with v_r(γ) := ∏_δ v_η(γ_δ)^{r_δ}. Moreover v_r is a multiplier system of weight k on Γ₀(N) in the sense of MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.7 (for k ∈ ℤ a character of Γ₀(N)), so η_r transforms like a modular form of weight k and multiplier v_r on Γ₀(N).
hypotheses: δ ∣ N and δ > 0 for all δ ∈ supp r; γ ∈ Γ₀(N); principal branch of (cτ + d)^{1/2}.
proofSteps: For each δ: η(δ·γτ) = η(γ_δ(δτ)) = v_η(γ_δ)·j(γ_δ, δτ)^{1/2}·η(δτ) = v_η(γ_δ)·(cτ + d)^{1/2}·η(δτ) (QM.1/gamma0-dilate, QM.1/eta-transformation-law).
Raise to r_δ and multiply over δ; ((cτ + d)^{1/2})^{Σ r_δ} collects the automorphy factor.
The multiplier-system property follows as in QM.1/eta-multiplier-is-multiplier-system from η_r ≠ 0 (API etaQuotient_ne_zero) and the cocycle of j.

nodes.title: η(δτ) at an arbitrary cusp (Hermite decomposition)
nodes.statement: Let δ ≥ 1 and σ = (a b; c d) ∈ SL(2, ℤ). Put A = gcd(c, δ) and D = δ/A. There are σ′ ∈ SL(2, ℤ) and B ∈ ℤ with 0 ≤ B < D such that diag(δ, 1)·σ = σ′·(A B; 0 D), and then for τ ∈ ℍ: η(δ·στ) = v_η(σ′)·D^{−1/2}·(cτ + d)^{1/2}·η((Aτ + B)/D). In particular (cτ + d)^{−1/2}η(δστ) has leading term v_η(σ′)D^{−1/2}e^{πiB/(12D)}·q^{A/(24D)}, and A/(24D) = gcd(c, δ)²/(24δ).
hypotheses: δ ≥ 1; σ ∈ SL(2, ℤ); principal branches (D > 0, so ((cτ + d)/D)^{1/2} = D^{−1/2}(cτ + d)^{1/2}).
proofSteps: The first column (δa, c) of diag(δ, 1)σ has gcd A = gcd(δ, c) (gcd(a, c) = 1); complete (δa/A, c/A) to σ′ ∈ SL(2, ℤ) by Bézout (Int.gcd_eq_gcd_ab); then σ′^{−1}diag(δ, 1)σ is upper triangular with determinant δ and diagonal (A, D); reduce B mod D by right multiplication of σ′ by a power of T.
δ·στ = σ′((Aτ + B)/D) and j(σ′, (Aτ + B)/D)·D = j(diag(δ,1)σ, τ) = cτ + d.
Apply QM.1/eta-transformation-law to σ′ at (Aτ + B)/D ∈ ℍ; the leading term follows from QM.1/eta-product-tendsto-one.

nodes.title: Ligozat's cusp-order formula for eta quotients
nodes.statement: Let r : ℕ →₀ ℤ be supported on positive integers, k = (1/2)Σ r_δ, and σ = (a b; c d) ∈ SL(2, ℤ). Put ρ_σ(r) := (1/24)·Σ_δ r_δ·gcd(c, δ)²/δ ∈ ℚ. Then there is C ≠ 0 with e^{−2πiρ_σ(r)τ}·((cτ + d)^{1/2})^{−2k}·η_r(στ) → C as Im τ → ∞: η_r has order exactly ρ_σ(r) (in q = e^{2πiτ}) at the cusp σ∞ = a/c. For Γ₀(N) with N a multiple of every δ, the cusp a/c (gcd(a, c) = 1) has width h_c = N/gcd(c², N), and the order in the local parameter q^{1/h_c} is h_c·ρ_σ(r) = (N/24)·Σ_δ gcd(c, δ)² r_δ/(gcd(c, N/c)·c·δ) when c ∣ N. Consequently η_r is holomorphic (resp. vanishes) at every cusp iff ρ_σ(r) ≥ 0 (resp. > 0) for every c ∣ N.
hypotheses: δ > 0 for δ ∈ supp r; σ ∈ SL(2, ℤ).
proofSteps: Apply QM.1/eta-dilate-slash to each factor η(δστ)^{r_δ}; the leading exponents gcd(c, δ)²/(24δ) add up to ρ_σ(r) and the leading coefficients multiply to a nonzero constant.
The width statement: the stabiliser of a/c in Γ₀(N) is generated (up to ±1) by σT^{h_c}σ^{−1}, with h_c = N/gcd(c², N) (standard computation with Γ₀(N)); the order in q^{1/h_c} is h_c·ρ.
acceptance: θ = η(2τ)⁵η(τ)^{−2}η(4τ)^{−2} on Γ₀(4): orders 0 at ∞ (c = 0: ρ = (10 − 2 − 8)/24), 0 at the cusp 0 (c = 1: ρ = (5/2 − 2 − 1/2)/24) and 1/4 at the cusp 1/2 (c = 2: ρ = (10 − 2 − 2)/24): θ vanishes only at 1/2.
Δ = η^{24}: order 1 at every cusp.
η(τ)²η(11τ)² on Γ₀(11): ρ = 1 at ∞ (c = 0) and ρ = (2 + 2/11)/24 = 1/11 at the cusp 0 (c = 1, width 11, local order 1): a cusp form.

sources.excerpt: and so for f to be holomorphic at the cusps it is necessary and sufficient that Σ_{0<m|N} ((c, m)²/m) r_m ≥ 0 for all c | N, with strict inequality in order that f be a cusp form. This observation is often attributed to [Lig].

nodes.title: θ = η(2τ)⁵/(η(τ)²η(4τ)²)
nodes.statement: For τ ∈ ℍ: Σ_{n∈ℤ} e^{2πin²τ} (= jacobiTheta(2τ), Shimura's θ) equals the eta quotient η(2τ)⁵/(η(τ)²η(4τ)²), i.e. η_r with r = −2·[1] + 5·[2] − 2·[4].
hypotheses: τ ∈ ℍ.
proofSteps: By QM.1/jacobi-triple-product-analytic at z = 0 and 2τ: jacobiTheta(2τ) = ∏_{n≥1}(1 − q^{2n})(1 + q^{2n−1})², q = e^{2πiτ}.
Rewrite ∏(1 + q^{2n−1}) = ∏(1 − q^{2n})²/(∏(1 − qⁿ)∏(1 − q^{4n})) (split n by parity twice, as in Kong–Teo's proof of Theorem 3.1).
The q-power prefactors of η(2τ)⁵η(τ)^{−2}η(4τ)^{−2} cancel: (10 − 2 − 8)/24 = 0.
acceptance: Leading coefficients: both sides are 1 + 2q + 2q⁴ + ….
Checked numerically at τ = 0.21 + 0.93i to 30 digits.

Equivalently: the half-integral-weight multiplier of θ produced by QM.1 from the eta multiplier agrees with the theta multiplier that MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.7 uses to define classical half-integral-weight forms on Γ₀(4N).

nodes.title: Savitt's Jacobi-symbol formula for v_η on Γ₀(4)
nodes.statement: For γ = (a b; c d) ∈ Γ₀(4): v_η(γ) = (c/d)·e^{πiE/12} with E = ac(1 − d²) + d(b − c + 3) − 3 and the extended Jacobi symbol ((c/d) = sgn(c)(c/|d|) for d < 0, (0/±1) = 1).
proofSteps: Values on the generators: v_η(T) = e^{πi/12}, v_η(−1) = −i, v_η(T̄⁴) = e^{−πi/3} (Savitt Lemma 4.4; from QM.1/dedekind-eta-multiplier).

The right side ε′ satisfies ε′(γ′γ) = ε′(γ′)ε′(γ)σ(γ′, γ) for γ′ ∈ {T, T̄⁴, −1}, with σ the sign cocycle (Petersson's rule, MP.7): Savitt Lemmas 4.8, 4.9, 4.11 and Proposition 4.12, using Jacobi reciprocity and periodicity (jacobiSym.quadratic_reciprocity, jacobiSym.mod_right, jacobiSym.mul_left).
Both v_η and ε′ satisfy the same recursion on the generators of Γ₀(4) (QM.1/gamma0-four-generation), and v_η satisfies it by QM.1/eta-multiplier-is-multiplier-system; induct.

nodes.title: The theta group Γ_θ
nodes.statement: Γ_θ := {γ = (a b; c d) ∈ SL(2, ℤ) : a ≡ d, b ≡ c (mod 2)}, the matrices congruent to 1 or S modulo 2. It is a subgroup of index 3 containing Γ(2), S, T² and −1, generated by S and T², with Γ_θ = Γ(2) ⊔ Γ(2)S; it has two cusp classes, ∞ (width 2) and 1 (width 1). Mathlib's jacobiTheta (ϑ(τ) = Σ e^{πin²τ}) is a modular form of weight 1/2 on Γ_θ (QM.1/theta-transformation-theta-group).
proofSteps: Closure under products and inverses: reduction mod 2 is a homomorphism SL(2, ℤ) → SL(2, 𝔽₂) and {1, S̄} is a subgroup of SL(2, 𝔽₂) ≅ S₃; Γ_θ is its preimage.
Index 3 = [SL(2, 𝔽₂) : {1, S̄}] = 6/2 (Mathlib's Subgroup.index and surjectivity of reduction).
Generation by S and T²: Γ_θ = Γ(2) ⊔ Γ(2)S and Γ(2) = ⟨T², ST²S^{−1}, −1⟩ (Euclidean descent as for Γ₀(4)).
Cusps: SL(2, ℤ) = Γ_θ ⊔ Γ_θT ⊔ Γ_θTS (QM.1/theta-group-cosets); T ∉ Γ_θ, T² ∈ Γ_θ give width 2 at ∞; (TS)^{−1}Γ_θ(TS) ∋ T gives width 1 at 1.
acceptance: [SL(2, ℤ) : Γ_θ] = 3 = 2 + 1 (sum of cusp widths).
Γ_θ ≠ Γ₀(2) (S ∉ Γ₀(2)) although both have index 3; they are conjugate in SL(2, ℤ).

nodes.title: Right cosets of Γ_θ and its two cusp classes
nodes.statement: For σ = (a b; c d) ∈ SL(2, ℤ): σ ∈ Γ_θ·T^ℤ ⟺ a + c is odd, and σ ∈ Γ_θ·(TS)·T^ℤ ⟺ a and c are both odd. Hence SL(2, ℤ) = Γ_θ ⊔ Γ_θT ⊔ Γ_θTS and the cusps of Γ_θ are the classes of ∞ (a/c with a + c odd) and of 1 (a/c with a, c odd).

Values: v_θ(S) = e^{−πi/4}, v_θ(T²) = 1, v_θ(−1) = −i; on Γ(2), v_θ(γ) = (2c/d)·ε_d^{−1} (extended Jacobi symbol, ε_d = 1 or i as d ≡ 1 or 3 mod 4), which is Shimura's multiplier of MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.7 transported by τ ↦ τ/2. Off Γ_θ the value is the junk value of the formula and carries no meaning.

nodes.title: jacobiTheta₂(τ/2, τ) → 2 at i∞
nodes.statement: As Im τ → ∞: jacobiTheta₂(τ/2, τ) = Σ_n e^{πi(n² + n)τ} → 2.

proofSteps: jacobiTheta₂(τ/2, τ) = Σ_n e^{πin(n+1)τ}; the terms n = 0, −1 equal 1 and the others are bounded by e^{−2π Im τ·|…|} (norm_jacobiTheta₂_term_le), summing to O(e^{−2π Im τ}).

nodes.title: ϑ at every cusp of Γ_θ
nodes.statement: For σ = (a b; c d) ∈ SL(2, ℤ): (i) if a + c is odd (σ∞ Γ_θ-equivalent to ∞), (cτ + d)^{−1/2}ϑ(στ) → C ≠ 0 as Im τ → ∞ (ϑ has order 0); (ii) if a and c are both odd (σ∞ equivalent to 1), e^{−πiτ/4}(cτ + d)^{−1/2}ϑ(στ) → C ≠ 0 (order 1/8 in q = e^{2πiτ}; the cusp 1 has width 1). Together with QM.1/jacobi-theta-nonvanishing this is the complete divisor of ϑ on Γ_θ\ℍ*: a zero of order 1/8 at the cusp 1 and nothing else.
hypotheses: σ ∈ SL(2, ℤ); principal branches.
proofSteps: (i) σ = γT^j with γ ∈ Γ_θ (QM.1/theta-group-cosets): (cτ + d)^{−1/2}ϑ(στ) = v_θ(γ)ϑ(τ + j) (QM.1/theta-transformation-theta-group, j(σ, τ) = j(γ, τ + j)) → v_θ(γ) (isBigO_at_im_infty_jacobiTheta_sub_one).

(ii) σ = γ·TS·T^j: (cτ + d)^{−1/2}ϑ(στ) = ±v_θ(γ)·τ′^{−1/2}ϑ(TSτ′) with τ′ = τ + j (sign cocycle, a constant), = ±v_θ(γ)e^{−πi/4}e^{πiτ′/4}jacobiTheta₂(τ′/2, τ′) (QM.1/theta-TS-slash) and jacobiTheta₂(τ′/2, τ′) → 2 (QM.1/theta-half-period-limit).

nodes.title: Fourier expansion of periodic holomorphic functions
nodes.statement: Let y₀ ∈ ℝ ∪ {−∞} and f holomorphic on {Im z > y₀} with f(z + 1) = f(z). For n ∈ ℤ and any y > y₀ put a_n := ∫₀¹ f(x + iy)e^{−2πin(x+iy)} dx (independent of y). Then f(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ} a_n e^{2πinz} for Im z > y₀, the series converging absolutely and locally uniformly; f is determined by (a_n).
hypotheses: f holomorphic and 1-periodic on the half-plane (or on ℂ, taking y₀ arbitrary).
proofSteps: Independence of y: apply the Cauchy–Goursat theorem on the rectangle [0, 1] × [y, y′] to f(z)e^{−2πinz} (Complex.integral_boundary_rect_eq_zero_of_differentiableOn); the vertical sides cancel by periodicity.

For fixed y, x ↦ f(x + iy) is a smooth 1-periodic function; two integrations by parts (fourierCoeffOn_of_hasDerivAt) give |a_n e^{−2πny}| ≤ C_y/n², so the Fourier coefficients are summable and the Fourier series converges pointwise to f (has_pointwise_sum_fourier_series_of_summable).
Absolute and locally uniform convergence on {Im z ≥ y + ε}: |a_n e^{2πinz}| = |a_n e^{−2πny}|·e^{−2πn(Im z − y)} for n ≥ 0, and symmetrically with a height y′ > Im z for n < 0.
acceptance: f(z) = e^{2πiz}: a_1 = 1, all other a_n = 0.
For f = jacobiTheta₂(·, τ) (entire, 1-periodic in z): a_n = e^{πin²τ}.

nodes.title: The analytic Jacobi triple product
nodes.statement: For τ ∈ ℍ and z ∈ ℂ: jacobiTheta₂(z, τ) = Σ_n e^{2πinz + πin²τ} = ∏_{n≥1}(1 − e^{2πinτ})(1 + e^{πi(2n−1)τ}e^{2πiz})(1 + e^{πi(2n−1)τ}e^{−2πiz}), the product converging absolutely.
hypotheses: τ ∈ ℍ (|w| < 1 for w = e^{πiτ}); z ∈ ℂ.
proofSteps: Let F(z) be the product. It is entire in z, 1-periodic, and F(z + τ) = e^{−πiτ − 2πiz}F(z) (shift the factors (1 + w^{2n−1}ζ) ↦ (1 + w^{2n+1}ζ)).

Expand F(z) = Σ a_n(τ)e^{2πinz} (QM.1/periodic-holomorphic-fourier-expansion); the quasi-periodicity gives a_{n+1} = w^{2n+1}a_n, so F = a₀(τ)·jacobiTheta₂(z, τ) (jacobiTheta₂_add_left' shows jacobiTheta₂ satisfies the same law).
a₀(w⁴) = a₀(w): evaluate at z = 1/8 and z = 1/4 (with τ ↦ 4τ) and compare the two resulting series Σ(−1)ⁿw^{4n²}, splitting the products by residues mod 4 and mod 8 (Kong–Teo Theorem 3.1).
a₀ is continuous at w = 0 with a₀(0) = 1, and w^{4^k} → 0, so a₀ ≡ 1.
acceptance: z = 0: jacobiTheta(τ) = ∏(1 − w^{2n})(1 + w^{2n−1})²; z = 1/2 with τ ↦ 3τ, z ↦ (τ + 1)/2 gives Euler's pentagonal theorem (Mathlib's Pentagonal.eulerFunction_eq_tprod) — a consistency check, not a dependency.

sources.excerpt: (Jacobi Triple Product Identity). When w and z are complex numbers with |w| < 1 and z ≠ 0, Π_{n=1}^∞ (1 − w^{2n})(1 + w^{2n−1}z²)(1 + w^{2n−1}z^{−2}) = Σ_{n=−∞}^{∞} w^{n²}z^{2n}.
sources.match: Same identity with w = e^{πiτ}, z = e^{πiz} (Corollary 3.2); proof followed step by step, the power-series expansion in z made precise by the Fourier lemma.

sources.excerpt: For any complex numbers τ and z with Im τ > 0, Π_{n=1}^∞ (1 − e^{2πinτ})(1 + e^{πi(2n−1)τ}e^{2πiz})(1 + e^{πi(2n−1)τ}e^{−2πiz}) = Σ e^{πin²τ}e^{2πinz}.
sources.match: Exactly our statement.

nodes.title: Zwegers' Jacobi theta function ϑ(z; τ)
nodes.statement: For z ∈ ℂ and τ ∈ ℍ: ϑ(z; τ) := Σ_{ν ∈ 1/2 + ℤ} e^{πiν²τ + 2πiν(z + 1/2)} = e^{πiτ/4 + πi(z + 1/2)}·jacobiTheta₂(z + 1/2 + τ/2, τ) (Mathlib's jacobiTheta₂). It is holomorphic on ℂ × ℍ, odd in z, and satisfies Zwegers' Proposition 1.3 (1)–(10): the elliptic law (QM.1/jacobi-theta-elliptic), ϑ(z; τ + 1) = e^{πi/4}ϑ(z; τ), ϑ(z/τ; −1/τ) = −i(−iτ)^{1/2}e^{πiz²/τ}ϑ(z; τ), the triple product (QM.1/jacobi-theta-triple-product), zeros exactly at ℤτ + ℤ (QM.1/jacobi-theta-zeros), ϑ′(0; τ) = −2πη(τ)³ (QM.1/jacobi-theta-derivative) and the modular law with multiplier v_η³ (QM.1/jacobi-theta-transformation). Convention (pinned): this is Zwegers' normalisation; the classical ϑ₁(z|τ) = Σ(−1)ⁿq^{(n+1/2)²/2}ζ^{n+1/2} used by Dabholkar–Murthy–Zagier equals −i·ϑ(z; τ).
hypotheses: τ ∈ ℍ (for Im τ ≤ 0 Mathlib's jacobiTheta₂ has junk value 0).
proofSteps: Define by the series; the identity with jacobiTheta₂ is the substitution ν = n + 1/2: πiν²τ + 2πiν(z + 1/2) = πin²τ + 2πin(z + 1/2 + τ/2) + πiτ/4 + πi(z + 1/2).
Holomorphy from Mathlib's hasFDerivAt_jacobiTheta₂; oddness from jacobiTheta₂_neg_left and the elliptic law.
(6): e^{πiν²} = e^{πi/4} for ν ∈ 1/2 + ℤ. (7): jacobiTheta₂_functional_equation applied at (z + 1/2 + τ/2, τ) and re-indexed.
acceptance: ϑ(0; τ) = 0; ϑ(1/2; τ) = −e^{πiτ/4}jacobiTheta₂(τ/2, τ) = −ϑ₂(τ); e^{−πiτ/4}ϑ(z; τ) → −2 sin(πz) as Im τ → ∞ (all checked numerically).

nodes.title: Elliptic law of ϑ(z; τ)
nodes.statement: For z ∈ ℂ, τ ∈ ℍ and l, μ ∈ ℤ: ϑ(z + lτ + μ; τ) = (−1)^{l+μ}·e^{−πil²τ − 2πilz}·ϑ(z; τ) (Zwegers 1.3 (1), (2)).
hypotheses: τ ∈ ℍ.
proofSteps: μ-shift: jacobiTheta₂_add_left and e^{πi(μ)} = (−1)^μ from the prefactor e^{πi(z+1/2)}.
τ-shift: jacobiTheta₂_add_left' gives ϑ(z + τ) = −e^{−πiτ−2πiz}ϑ(z); iterate l times (induction on l ∈ ℤ, both directions).

nodes.title: Uniqueness of ϑ(·; τ) by its quasi-periodicities
nodes.statement: Let τ ∈ ℍ and f entire with f(z + 1) = −f(z) and f(z + τ) = −e^{−πiτ − 2πiz}f(z) for all z. Then f = C·ϑ(·; τ) for a constant C.
hypotheses: τ ∈ ℍ; f entire.
proofSteps: g(z) := e^{πiz}f(z) is entire and 1-periodic; by QM.1/periodic-holomorphic-fourier-expansion, g(z) = Σ a_n e^{2πinz}.
g(z + τ) = −e^{−2πiz}g(z) gives a_{n+1} = −e^{2πinτ}a_n (compare Fourier coefficients), so a_n = (−1)ⁿe^{πin(n−1)τ}a_0 for all n ∈ ℤ: the solutions form a space of dimension ≤ 1.
ϑ(·; τ) is a solution (QM.1/jacobi-theta-elliptic) and nonzero (the Fourier coefficients e^{πi(n−1/2)²τ + πi(n−1/2)} of e^{πiz}ϑ(z; τ) are nonzero), so f = C·ϑ(·; τ).
acceptance: f = ϑ(·; τ) itself gives C = 1; f = 0 gives C = 0; e^{πiz} (1-antiperiodic but violating the τ-law) is excluded.

nodes.title: Modular transformation of ϑ(z; τ) with multiplier v_η³
nodes.statement: For γ = (a b; c d) ∈ SL(2, ℤ), τ ∈ ℍ, z ∈ ℂ: ϑ(z/(cτ + d); γτ) = v_η(γ)³·(cτ + d)^{1/2}·e^{πicz²/(cτ + d)}·ϑ(z; τ) (principal branch).
hypotheses: γ ∈ SL(2, ℤ), τ ∈ ℍ.
proofSteps: F(z) := e^{−πicz²/(cτ+d)}ϑ(z/(cτ + d); γτ) is entire. From 1/(cτ + d) = a − c·γτ and τ/(cτ + d) = d·γτ − b, F(z + 1) and F(z + τ) are obtained from QM.1/jacobi-theta-elliptic at γτ with (l, μ) = (−c, a), resp. (d, −b); simplifying the exponentials with ad − bc = 1 gives F(z + 1) = −F(z) and F(z + τ) = −e^{−πiτ−2πiz}F(z).
By QM.1/jacobi-theta-uniqueness, F = C(γ, τ)·ϑ(·; τ). Differentiate at z = 0: C(γ, τ) = ϑ′(0; γτ)/((cτ + d)ϑ′(0; τ)) = η(γτ)³/((cτ + d)η(τ)³) (QM.1/jacobi-theta-derivative).
By QM.1/eta-transformation-law, η(γτ)³ = v_η(γ)³((cτ + d)^{1/2})³η(τ)³, so C = v_η(γ)³(cτ + d)^{1/2}.

nodes.title: The modular slash action of weight k and index m
nodes.statement: For k, m ∈ ½ℤ, γ = (a b; c d) ∈ SL(2, ℤ) and φ : ℍ × ℂ → ℂ: (φ|_{k,m}γ)(τ, z) := (cτ + d)^{−k}·e(−mcz²/(cτ + d))·φ(γτ, z/(cτ + d)), e(x) = e^{2πix}, principal branch of (cτ + d)^{−k}. For k ∈ ℤ this is a right action of SL(2, ℤ) ((φ|γ₁)|γ₂ = φ|γ₁γ₂); for k ∈ ½ + ℤ it is an action up to MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.7's sign cocycle σ(γ₁, γ₂)^{2k}. nodes.title: The Jacobi group law for the two slash actions
nodes.statement: For k, m ∈ ½ℤ, γ = (a b; c d) ∈ SL(2, ℤ), (l, μ) ∈ ℤ² and φ: (φ|_m[l, μ])|_{k,m}γ = (φ|_{k,m}γ)|_m[(l, μ)γ] with (l, μ)γ = (la + μc, lb + μd). Hence the pairs (γ, X) ∈ SL(2, ℤ) × ℤ² act through the semidirect product SL(2, ℤ) ⋉ ℤ² with (γ, X)(γ′, X′) = (γγ′, Xγ′ + X′) (Eichler–Zagier's Jacobi group), for k ∈ ℤ and 2m ∈ ℤ.
hypotheses: 2m ∈ ℤ; k ∈ ℤ for the group-action statement.
proofSteps: With (l′, μ′) = (l, μ)γ: (l′τ + μ′)/(cτ + d) = l·γτ + μ, from 1/(cτ + d) = a − c·γτ and τ/(cτ + d) = d·γτ − b; so both sides evaluate φ at (γτ, z/(cτ + d) + lγτ + μ), and the exponential factors agree by a direct computation using ad − bc = 1.

nodes.title: Jacobi forms of weight k and index m
nodes.statement: J_{k,m}(v, χ) is the ℂ-subspace of functions φ : ℍ × ℂ → ℂ holomorphic (jointly, as a function on {Im τ > 0} × ℂ), with φ|_{k,m}γ = v(γ)·φ for all γ ∈ SL(2, ℤ) and φ|_m[l, μ] = χ(l, μ)·φ for all (l, μ) ∈ ℤ², where k, m ∈ ½ℤ, v is a multiplier system of weight k on SL(2, ℤ) (MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.7; v ≡ 1 when k ∈ ℤ and there is no multiplier) and χ : ℤ² → ℂ^× a character (χ ≡ 1 for Eichler–Zagier forms), such that for all α, β ∈ ℚ the function τ ↦ e(mα²τ)·φ(τ, ατ + β) is bounded as Im τ → ∞. The Eichler–Zagier space of (holomorphic) Jacobi forms on SL(2, ℤ) ⋉ ℤ² is J_{k,m} := J_{k,m}(1, 1) with k ∈ ℤ, m ∈ ℕ; for these, membership is equivalent to c(n, r) = 0 unless 4nm ≥ r² (QM.1/jacobi-fourier-support, DMZ (4.5)). Convention (pinned): the growth condition is DMZ's second characterisation (bounded along all rational torsion points), which makes sense with multipliers; the Fourier condition is a theorem.
hypotheses: k, m ∈ ℚ with 2k, 2m ∈ ℤ; v : SL(2, ℤ) → ℂ; χ : ℤ² → ℂ.
For index m ≥ 1 and trivial v, χ, the space is Eichler–Zagier's; index 0 gives M_k(SL(2, ℤ)).
proofSteps: Closure under addition and scalars: every condition is linear.
Products: J_{k,m}(v, χ)·J_{k′,m′}(v′, χ′) ⊆ J_{k+k′,m+m′}(vv′σ, χχ′) (σ ≡ 1 for integral weights): the slash factors multiply and the growth bounds multiply.

Index 0: elliptic invariance makes z ↦ φ(τ, z) an entire function invariant under ℤτ + ℤ, hence bounded and constant (Liouville, Differentiable.apply_eq_apply_of_bounded), so J_{k,0} ≅ M_k(SL(2, ℤ)) (Mathlib's ModularForm; boundedness at every cusp by OnePoint.isBoundedAt_iff_forall_SL2Z).
acceptance: J_{k,1} = 0 for k odd (c(n, −r) = (−1)^kc(n, r) and r ≡ −r mod 2); J_{−2,1} = 0 while the weak space is spanned by φ_{−2,1}; the constant 1 lies in J_{0,0}.

nodes.title: Jacobi cusp forms
nodes.statement: J⁰_{k,m}(v, χ) is the ℂ-subspace of functions φ : ℍ × ℂ → ℂ holomorphic (jointly, as a function on {Im τ > 0} × ℂ), with φ|_{k,m}γ = v(γ)·φ for all γ ∈ SL(2, ℤ) and φ|_m[l, μ] = χ(l, μ)·φ for all (l, μ) ∈ ℤ², where k, m ∈ ½ℤ, v is a multiplier system of weight k on SL(2, ℤ) (MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.7; v ≡ 1 when k ∈ ℤ and there is no multiplier) and χ : ℤ² → ℂ^× a character (χ ≡ 1 for Eichler–Zagier forms), such that for all α, β ∈ ℚ, e(mα²τ)·φ(τ, ατ + β) → 0 as Im τ → ∞. For v, χ trivial and k ∈ ℤ, m ≥ 1: membership ⟺ c(n, r) = 0 unless 4nm > r² (DMZ (4.6)).

proofSteps: Linear conditions; J⁰ ⊆ J since a function tending to 0 is bounded.

nodes.title: Weak Jacobi forms
nodes.statement: J̃_{k,m}(v, χ) is the ℂ-subspace of functions φ : ℍ × ℂ → ℂ holomorphic (jointly, as a function on {Im τ > 0} × ℂ), with φ|_{k,m}γ = v(γ)·φ for all γ ∈ SL(2, ℤ) and φ|_m[l, μ] = χ(l, μ)·φ for all (l, μ) ∈ ℤ², where k, m ∈ ½ℤ, v is a multiplier system of weight k on SL(2, ℤ) (MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.7; v ≡ 1 when k ∈ ℤ and there is no multiplier) and χ : ℤ² → ℂ^× a character (χ ≡ 1 for Eichler–Zagier forms), such that for every fixed z ∈ ℂ the function τ ↦ φ(τ, z) is bounded as Im τ → ∞. For v, χ trivial and k ∈ ℤ: membership ⟺ c(n, r) = 0 unless n ≥ 0 (DMZ (4.7)).
hypotheses: As for QM.1/jacobi-form.
proofSteps: Linear conditions.

Fourier characterisation: for fixed z, φ(τ, z) = Σ_n (Σ_r c(n, r)ζ^r)qⁿ; boundedness for every z forces the Laurent polynomials Σ_r c(n, r)ζ^r (n < 0) to vanish identically (QM.1/jacobi-fourier-expansion).
acceptance: φ_{−2,1} and φ_{0,1} span the index-1 weak forms of weight ≤ 0 (DMZ §4.3); E₄ (independent of z) lies in J̃_{4,0}.

nodes.statement: J^!_{k,m}(v, χ) is the ℂ-subspace of functions φ : ℍ × ℂ → ℂ holomorphic (jointly, as a function on {Im τ > 0} × ℂ), with φ|_{k,m}γ = v(γ)·φ for all γ ∈ SL(2, ℤ) and φ|_m[l, μ] = χ(l, μ)·φ for all (l, μ) ∈ ℤ², where k, m ∈ ½ℤ, v is a multiplier system of weight k on SL(2, ℤ) (MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.7; v ≡ 1 when k ∈ ℤ and there is no multiplier) and χ : ℤ² → ℂ^× a character (χ ≡ 1 for Eichler–Zagier forms), such that for some N ∈ ℕ and every fixed z ∈ ℂ, τ ↦ e(Nτ)·φ(τ, z) is bounded as Im τ → ∞. For v, χ trivial: membership ⟺ c(n, r) = 0 unless n ≥ n₀ for some n₀ ∈ ℤ.

nodes.title: Fourier coefficients c(n, r) of a Jacobi form
nodes.statement: For φ : ℍ × ℂ → ℂ and n, r ∈ ℤ: c_φ(n, r) := ∫₀¹∫₀¹ φ(x + i, u)·e(−n(x + i) − ru) du dx. When φ is holomorphic and 1-periodic in τ and in z, φ(τ, z) = Σ_{n,r} c_φ(n, r)qⁿζ^r absolutely (QM.1/jacobi-fourier-expansion), and the integral may be taken at any height.
hypotheses: φ holomorphic and 1-periodic in both variables for the expansion; the integral is defined for every φ (junk 0 when not integrable).
proofSteps: Definition by the double integral (Mathlib's intervalIntegral).
Constant and monomial values by direct integration of e(jx) over [0, 1].

nodes.title: Fourier expansion in q and ζ
nodes.statement: If φ is holomorphic on ℍ × ℂ with φ(τ + 1, z) = φ(τ, z + 1) = φ(τ, z), then φ(τ, z) = Σ_{(n,r)∈ℤ²} c_φ(n, r)·e(nτ + rz), absolutely convergent and locally uniform, and c_φ(n, r) = ∫₀¹∫₀¹ φ(x + iy, u + iv)e(−n(x + iy) − r(u + iv)) du dx for every y > 0, v ∈ ℝ.
hypotheses: φ jointly holomorphic; 1-periodic in τ and in z.
proofSteps: Expand z ↦ φ(τ, z) (entire, 1-periodic) by QM.1/periodic-holomorphic-fourier-expansion: φ = Σ_r g_r(τ)ζ^r with g_r(τ) = ∫₀¹φ(τ, u + iv)e(−r(u + iv))du holomorphic and 1-periodic in τ.
Expand each g_r in τ by the same lemma on {Im τ > 0}; the double series converges absolutely because the bounds of the lemma are uniform on compacta (Cauchy estimates on a polyannulus in (q, ζ)).
acceptance: φ(τ, z) = jacobiTheta(2τ)·e(z) = Σ_n q^{n²}ζ: c(0, 1) = 1, c(n², 1) = 2 for n ≥ 1, all other c(n, r) = 0.

nodes.title: c(n, r) depends only on 4nm − r² and r mod 2m
nodes.statement: For m ≥ 1, k ∈ ℤ and φ ∈ J^!_{k,m}: c(n, r) = c(n′, r′) whenever 4nm − r² = 4n′m − r′² and r ≡ r′ (mod 2m); i.e. c(n, r) = C(4nm − r², r mod 2m). Moreover c(n, −r) = (−1)^k c(n, r).
hypotheses: m ≥ 1; trivial multiplier and character.
proofSteps: φ|_m[l, 0] = φ gives c(n, r) = c(n + lr + ml², r + 2ml) by comparing Fourier coefficients (uniqueness in QM.1/jacobi-fourier-expansion).
Every (n′, r′) with the same discriminant and r′ ≡ r (mod 2m) is of this form (r′ = r + 2ml).
φ|(−1) = φ gives φ(τ, −z) = (−1)^kφ(τ, z) (API jacobiModularSlash_neg_one), hence c(n, −r) = (−1)^kc(n, r).
acceptance: φ_{−2,1} (m = 1): c(0, 1) = c(2, 3) = C(−1) = 1 and c(1, 0) = c(2, 2) = C(4) = −12 (DMZ Table 1; checked numerically).

sources.excerpt: Equation (4.2) is then equivalent to the periodicity property c(n, r) = C(4nm − r², r), where C(∆, r) depends only on r (mod 2m) .

nodes.title: Fourier characterisation of holomorphic Jacobi forms
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℤ, m ≥ 1 and φ ∈ J^!_{k,m} (trivial multiplier and character): φ ∈ J_{k,m} ⟺ c(n, r) = 0 whenever 4nm < r². (The analogous statements for cusp forms, 4nm ≤ r², and weak forms, n < 0, are the API items mem_JacobiCuspForm_iff_fourierCoeff and mem_WeakJacobiForm_iff_fourierCoeff and are proved the same way.)
hypotheses: k ∈ ℤ, m ≥ 1; φ weakly holomorphic with trivial multiplier and character.
proofSteps: e(mα²τ)φ(τ, ατ + β) = Σ c(n, r)e(rβ)·e((n + rα + mα²)τ) and n + rα + mα² = (4nm − r²)/(4m) + m(α + r/(2m))² (QM.1/jacobi-fourier-expansion).
⇐: all exponents are ≥ 0 when every nonzero c(n, r) has 4nm ≥ r²; the series is dominated uniformly for Im τ ≥ 1, so it is bounded.

⇒: the discriminants of nonzero coefficients are bounded below (n ≥ n₀ and every class mod 2m has a representative |r| ≤ m, QM.1/jacobi-coefficient-discriminant). If some c(n, r) ≠ 0 has Δ = 4nm − r² < 0, choose one with Δ minimal and take α = −r/(2m), β = 0: every term has exponent Δ′/(4m) + (r′ − r)²/(4m) ≥ Δ/(4m), with equality only for (n′, r′) = (n, r), so e(mα²τ)φ(τ, ατ) = c(n, r)e(Δτ/(4m))(1 + o(1)) is unbounded.
acceptance: φ_{−2,1}: c(0, 1) = 1 with 4·0·1 − 1 < 0, so φ_{−2,1} ∉ J_{−2,1}; ϑ_{m,μ}-type terms with Δ = 0 are allowed.

f is holomorphic; the growth condition at α = β = 0 gives boundedness at i∞, hence at every cusp (OnePoint.isBoundedAt_iff_forall_SL2Z with slash invariance).

nodes.title: The index-m theta functions ϑ_{m,μ}
nodes.statement: For m ≥ 1 and μ ∈ ℤ: ϑ_{m,μ}(τ, z) := Σ_{r ≡ μ (mod 2m)} q^{r²/(4m)}ζ^r = Σ_{n∈ℤ} e((2mn + μ)²τ/(4m) + (2mn + μ)z) = e(μ²τ/(4m) + μz)·jacobiTheta₂(2mz + μτ, 2mτ). It depends only on μ mod 2m, is invariant under the index-m elliptic slash, and satisfies ϑ_{m,μ}(τ + 1, z) = e(μ²/(4m))ϑ_{m,μ}(τ, z) and the S-law of QM.1/theta-index-S.
proofSteps: Absolute convergence and the identity with jacobiTheta₂: (2mn + μ)²/(4m) = mn² + nμ + μ²/(4m) and the definition of jacobiTheta₂.
μ ↦ μ + 2m re-indexes n ↦ n + 1; the elliptic law: z ↦ z + lτ + μ′ shifts r ↦ r + 2ml… as in DMZ (4.4).

nodes.title: The S-law of ϑ_{m,μ}
nodes.statement: For m ≥ 1, μ ∈ ℤ, τ ∈ ℍ, z ∈ ℂ: ϑ_{m,μ}(−1/τ, z/τ) = (τ/(2mi))^{1/2}·e(mz²/τ)·Σ_{ν mod 2m} e(−μν/(2m))·ϑ_{m,ν}(τ, z) (principal branch).

The result is a theta series in τ/(2m); split its summation index by residues mod 2m to express it through the ϑ_{m,ν}(τ, z), producing the finite Fourier transform e(−μν/2m).

nodes.title: Theta decomposition of Jacobi forms
nodes.statement: Let m ≥ 1 and φ : ℍ × ℂ → ℂ with z ↦ φ(τ, z) entire for each τ and φ|_m[l, μ] = φ for all (l, μ) ∈ ℤ². Then for all τ, z: φ(τ, z) = Σ_{μ mod 2m} h_μ(τ)·ϑ_{m,μ}(τ, z), with h_μ = QM.1/theta-decomposition-coefficient; the h_μ are uniquely determined by this identity.
hypotheses: m ≥ 1; entire in z; index-m elliptic law with trivial character.
proofSteps: φ is 1-periodic in z ((l, μ) = (0, 1)); expand φ(τ, z) = Σ_r a_r(τ)ζ^r (QM.1/periodic-holomorphic-fourier-expansion) and set h_r(τ) = e(−r²τ/4m)a_r(τ).
(l, μ) = (1, 0) gives h_{r+2m} = h_r; group r by residues mod 2m to obtain Σ_μ h_μϑ_{m,μ} (QM.1/jacobi-theta-index).

nodes.title: The theta coefficients form a vector-valued modular form of weight k − 1/2
nodes.statement: Let k ∈ ℤ, m ≥ 1 and φ as in QM.1/theta-decomposition with moreover φ|_{k,m}γ = φ for all γ ∈ SL(2, ℤ). Then for every μ: h_μ(τ + 1) = e(−μ²/(4m))·h_μ(τ) and h_μ(−1/τ) = τ^k·(−iτ)^{−1/2}·(2m)^{−1/2}·Σ_{ν mod 2m} e(μν/(2m))·h_ν(τ) (principal branch).
hypotheses: k ∈ ℤ, m ≥ 1; trivial multiplier and character.
proofSteps: T: φ(τ + 1, z) = φ(τ, z) and QM.1/jacobi-theta-index (API jacobiThetaIndex_T); compare coefficients by QM.1/theta-index-linear-independence.

S: substitute the theta decomposition into φ(−1/τ, z/τ) = τ^ke(mz²/τ)φ(τ, z), apply QM.1/theta-index-S, compare coefficients of ϑ_{m,ν}(τ, z) (QM.1/theta-index-linear-independence), and invert the finite Fourier transform (Σ_ν e(μν/2m)e(−ν′ν/2m) = 2m·δ_{μν′}).

nodes.title: Holomorphy of φ versus boundedness of the h_μ
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℤ, m ≥ 1 and φ ∈ J^!_{k,m}: φ ∈ J_{k,m} ⟺ every h_μ is bounded as Im τ → ∞; φ ∈ J⁰_{k,m} ⟺ every h_μ → 0; φ ∈ J̃_{k,m} ⟺ h_μ(τ) = O(e^{2π Im τ·μ̄²/(4m)}) for every μ, with μ̄ the representative of μ mod 2m of least absolute value.
hypotheses: k ∈ ℤ, m ≥ 1; trivial multiplier and character.
proofSteps: By API thetaDecompositionCoeff_eq_tsum, h_μ = Σ_Δ C(Δ, μ)q^{Δ/4m}; bounded ⟺ C(Δ, μ) = 0 for Δ < 0 ⟺ (QM.1/jacobi-coefficient-discriminant) c(n, r) = 0 for 4nm < r² ⟺ φ ∈ J_{k,m} (QM.1/jacobi-fourier-support).

nodes.title: Vector-valued modular forms give Jacobi forms
nodes.statement: Let k ∈ ℤ, m ≥ 1 and h_μ : ℍ → ℂ (μ ∈ ℤ) with h_{μ+2m} = h_μ, satisfying the T-law h_μ(τ + 1) = e(−μ²/(4m))h_μ(τ) and the S-law of QM.1/theta-decomposition-transformation. Then φ := Σ_{μ mod 2m} h_μϑ_{m,μ} satisfies φ|_{k,m}γ = φ for every γ ∈ SL(2, ℤ) and φ|_m[l, μ′] = φ for all (l, μ′). With holomorphic h_μ this gives the isomorphisms J_{k,m} ≅ {h : holomorphic, the two laws, bounded} and J^!_{k,m} ≅ {h : holomorphic, the two laws, meromorphic at i∞} inverse to φ ↦ (h_μ).
proofSteps: Elliptic invariance: each ϑ_{m,μ} is invariant (API jacobiEllipticSlash_jacobiThetaIndex).
Invariance under T and S: combine the laws of h with API jacobiThetaIndex_T and QM.1/theta-index-S (finite Fourier inversion).
Invariance under all of SL(2, ℤ): the set of γ with φ|γ = φ is a subgroup (API jacobiModularSlash_mul) containing S and T, hence everything (SpecialLinearGroup.SL2Z_generators).
acceptance: The theta coefficients (h_0, h_1) of φ_{−2,1} (k = −2, m = 1) satisfy the hypotheses and return φ_{−2,1}.

nodes.title: Theta coefficients as modular forms for the Weil representation
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℤ, m ≥ 1 and φ ∈ J_{k,m} (resp. J^!_{k,m}), the vector h = Σ_{μ mod 2m} h_μe_μ ∈ ℂ[ℤ/2m] is a holomorphic (resp. weakly holomorphic) vector-valued modular form of weight k − 1/2 for the Weil representation ρ_{L(−1)} of Mp₂(ℤ) attached to the lattice L = ℤ with quadratic form q(x) = mx² (discriminant group L′/L = (1/2m)ℤ/ℤ ≅ ℤ/2m, q(μ/2m) = μ²/(4m)), i.e. for the dual Weil representation of (ℤ, mx²), in the convention of MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.7: h(γτ) = φ_γ(τ)^{2k−1}ρ_{L(−1)}(γ̃)h(τ) for γ̃ = (γ, φ_γ) ∈ Mp₂(ℤ). proofSteps: On generators: ρ_{L(−1)}(T̃)e_μ = e(−μ²/4m)e_μ and ρ_{L(−1)}(S̃)e_μ = e^{πi/4}(2m)^{−1/2}Σ_ν e(μν/2m)e_ν (AAW (3.2) with signature (0, 1)); with φ_S(τ) = τ^{1/2}, τ^{k−1/2}e^{πi/4} = τ^k(−iτ)^{−1/2}, which is QM.1/theta-decomposition-transformation.
Mp₂(ℤ) is generated by T̃ and S̃ (MP.7), so the generator laws determine the transformation under all of Mp₂(ℤ); the converse is QM.1/theta-decomposition-converse.

nodes.title: The partition generating function on the unit disc
nodes.statement: Write p(n) = #(Nat.Partition n) for the number of partitions of n ∈ ℕ (Mathlib's `Nat.Partition`, so p(0) = 1). The partition generating function is F(x) = Σ_{n≥0} p(n) xⁿ for x ∈ ℂ (Mathlib's `tsum`). For |x| < 1: the series converges absolutely; F(x) = ∏_{m≥1} (1 − xᵐ)⁻¹, the product converging in the sense of Mathlib's `HasProd`; F(x) ≠ 0; F is holomorphic on the open unit disc; |F(x)| ≤ F(|x|); and on [0, 1) the function F is real, at least 1 and strictly increasing. F(0) = 1. No statement is made for |x| ≥ 1, where the `tsum` convention applies.
hypotheses: All analytic statements assume |x| < 1; the definition itself is total.
p(n) is Mathlib's Fintype.card (Nat.Partition n); partitions of n are multisets of positive integers with sum n.
proofSteps: Partial products: for M ≥ 1 and |x| < 1, ∏_{m≤M}(1 − xᵐ)⁻¹ = ∏_{m≤M} Σ_{j≥0} x^{mj} (geometric series, `hasSum_geometric_of_norm_lt_one`); multiplying out the finitely many absolutely convergent series gives Σ_n p_{≤M}(n) xⁿ, where p_{≤M}(n) counts partitions of n with all parts ≤ M; the coefficient count is the case f = 1 of `Nat.Partition.hasProd_genFun` restricted to the parts ≤ M.

Absolute convergence: p_{≤M}(n) = p(n) for n ≤ M, so for 0 ≤ r < 1, Σ_{n≤M} p(n) rⁿ ≤ ∏_{m≤M}(1 − rᵐ)⁻¹ ≤ ∏_{m≥1}(1 − rᵐ)⁻¹, which is finite because ∏(1 − rᵐ) converges to a nonzero limit (`ModularForm.multipliable_one_sub_pow`, `tprod_one_add_ne_zero_of_summable`).

Product formula: for |x| < 1 the partial products Σ_n p_{≤M}(n) xⁿ converge to Σ_n p(n) xⁿ by dominated convergence (|p_{≤M}(n) xⁿ| ≤ p(n)|x|ⁿ); they also converge to ∏_{m≥1}(1 − xᵐ)⁻¹, the inverse of the nonzero convergent product.
Holomorphy: F is a power series whose radius of convergence is at least 1 by the previous step.
|F(x)| ≤ F(|x|), F ≥ 1 and strict monotonicity on [0, 1): all coefficients p(n) are ≥ 1.
acceptance: F(0) = 1 and the Taylor coefficients of F at 0 are 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 15 (p(7) = 15, Kong–Teo p. 1).
F(e^{2πiτ}) = e^{πiτ/12}/η(τ) for τ in the upper half-plane (node partition-generating-function-eq-eta).

nodes.title: The partition function is nondecreasing
nodes.statement: For every m ∈ ℕ, p(m) ≤ p(m + 1). Consequently p(m) ≤ p(m′) whenever m ≤ m′, and p(m) ≤ p(24m − 1) for every m ≥ 1.

nodes.title: Transformation of the partition generating function near a root of unity
nodes.statement: Let k ≥ 1 and h ∈ ℤ with gcd(h, k) = 1, and let H ∈ ℤ satisfy hH ≡ −1 (mod k). For every z ∈ ℂ with Re z > 0, F(exp(2πih/k − 2πz/k²)) = exp(πi·s(h, k)) · (z/k)^{1/2} · exp(π/(12z) − πz/(12k²)) · F(exp(2πiH/k − 2π/z)), where s(h, k) is the Dedekind sum of QM.1 and (z/k)^{1/2} is the principal square root (Re(z/k) > 0).
hypotheses: k ≥ 1, gcd(h, k) = 1, hH ≡ −1 (mod k), Re z > 0.
Both arguments of F lie in the unit disc: |exp(−2πz/k²)| = exp(−2π Re z/k²) < 1 and |exp(−2π/z)| = exp(−2π Re(1/z)) < 1.
proofSteps: Put τ = h/k + iz/k² ∈ ℍ and choose K ∈ ℤ with kK − hH = 1; then γ = (H, −K; k, −h) ∈ SL₂(ℤ) with lower-left entry k > 0, and γτ = H/k + i/z.
Apply the eta transformation law of QM.1 (for c > 0: η(γτ) = exp(πi((a + d)/(12c) + s(−d, c))) (−i(cτ + d))^{1/2} η(τ), principal branch) with c = k, d = −h: s(−d, c) = s(h, k) and −i(kτ − h) = z/k.

Rewrite η(τ)⁻¹ and η(γτ)⁻¹ by partition-generating-function-eq-eta; the exponentials combine to exp(π/(12z) − πz/(12k²)) since πiτ/12 − πiγτ/12 + πi(H − h)/(12k) collapses (the H- and h-terms cancel).
Periodicity F(e^{2πi(τ+1)}) = F(e^{2πiτ}) shows that the right side depends on H only modulo k.

nodes.title: Two Ford circles are tangent or disjoint
nodes.statement: Let a/b ≠ c/d be rationals in lowest terms (b, d ≥ 1). Then C(a, b) and C(c, d) are either externally tangent or disjoint; they are tangent iff |bc − ad| = 1. In particular Ford circles at consecutive terms of a Farey sequence F_N are tangent.
hypotheses: a/b ≠ c/d, both in lowest terms with positive denominators.
proofSteps: Let D be the distance between the centres and S = 1/(2b²) + 1/(2d²) the sum of the radii; compute D² − S² = ((bc − ad)² − 1)/(b²d²).
bc − ad ≠ 0 since the fractions differ, so (bc − ad)² ≥ 1 and D ≥ S, with equality iff |bc − ad| = 1.
For consecutive terms of F_N, bc − ad = 1 by ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.2/farey-neighbour-property.

sources.excerpt: Theorem 2.10. Two distinct Ford circles C(a, b) and C(c, d) are either tangent to each other or disjoint. They are tangent if and only if bc −ad = ±1.

If h/k < h₂/k₂ with kh₂ − hk₂ = 1, the tangency point of C(h, k) and C(h₂, k₂) is α₂(h, k) = h/k + k₂/(k(k² + k₂²)) + i/(k² + k₂²).

nodes.title: The local coordinate at a Ford circle
nodes.statement: Let h/k be in lowest terms and let w = −ik²(τ − h/k), i.e. τ = h/k + iw/k². This affine map sends C(h, k) onto the circle K = {w : |w − 1/2| = 1/2}, the point h/k to 0 and the real axis to the imaginary axis. If h₁/k₁ < h/k < h₂/k₂ with hk₁ − kh₁ = 1 = kh₂ − hk₂, it sends α₁(h, k) to w₁ = k²/(k² + k₁²) + i·kk₁/(k² + k₁²) and α₂(h, k) to w₂ = k²/(k² + k₂²) − i·kk₂/(k² + k₂²), and the arc of C(h, k) from α₁ to α₂ not containing h/k onto the arc of K from w₁ to w₂ not containing 0, traversed clockwise when the arc of C(h, k) is traversed from α₁ to α₂.
hypotheses: hk₁ − kh₁ = 1 and kh₂ − hk₂ = 1.
proofSteps: The map is a similarity (rotation by −π/2 composed with scaling by k² and a translation): it sends the centre h/k + i/(2k²) to 1/2 and multiplies the radius by k².
Evaluate at α₁, α₂ from ford-circle-tangency-point.
The real axis maps to the imaginary axis, so the arc avoiding h/k maps to the arc avoiding 0; orientation follows from the rotation by −π/2.

nodes.title: Estimates on the chords of the Rademacher path
nodes.statement: Let N ≥ 1 and let h₁/k₁ < h/k < h₂/k₂ be consecutive terms of the Farey sequence F_N extended periodically (so that 1/1 has right neighbour (N + 1)/N), and let w₁, w₂ be as in ford-circle-local-coordinate. Then |w₁| = k/√(k² + k₁²) and |w₂| = k/√(k² + k₂²); every w on the segment [w₁, w₂] satisfies |w| ≤ √2·k/(N + 1), Re w ≥ k²/(2N²) and Re(1/w) > 1/4; the segment has length at most 2√2·k/(N + 1).
hypotheses: Consecutive terms of F_N (with the periodic extension at the ends).
proofSteps: |w₁|² = (k⁴ + k²k₁²)/(k² + k₁²)² = k²/(k² + k₁²).
k + k₁ ≥ N + 1 and k + k₂ ≥ N + 1 by ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.2/farey-neighbour-property; hence k² + k₁² ≥ (k + k₁)²/2 ≥ (N + 1)²/2, and likewise for k₂.
By convexity |w| ≤ max(|w₁|, |w₂|) ≤ √2·k/(N + 1) on the segment, and the length is at most |w₁| + |w₂|.
Re w is a convex combination of k²/(k² + k₁²) and k²/(k² + k₂²), each ≥ k²/(2N²) since k, k₁, k₂ ≤ N.
acceptance: N = 1, h/k = 1/1 with neighbours 0/1 and 2/1: w₁ = 1/2 + i/2, w₂ = 1/2 − i/2, |w| ≤ 1/√2 = √2/(N + 1) on the chord, Re(1/w) ≥ 1 > 1/4.

nodes.title: Minor arcs of the model circle
nodes.statement: Let w ∈ K = {|w − 1/2| = 1/2} and let W be the minor arc of K from 0 to w. Then the length of W is at most π|w|/2, and |z| ≤ |w| for every z ∈ W.
hypotheses: w ∈ K; for w = 0 the arc is a point.
proofSteps: Write z = (1 + e^{iθ})/2, so |z| = cos(θ/2) for θ ∈ [0, π]; by symmetry take θ_w ∈ [0, π).
The arc has length (π − θ_w)/2 and |w| = sin((π − θ_w)/2); Jordan's inequality sin t ≥ (2/π)t on [0, π/2] (`Real.mul_le_sin`) gives length ≤ π|w|/2.
|z| = cos(θ/2) is decreasing in θ ∈ [θ_w, π], so |z| ≤ |w| on W.
acceptance: w = 1: the arc is a half circle of length π/2 = π|w|/2 (equality).

nodes.title: The Rademacher path P(N)
nodes.statement: For N ≥ 1 let 0/1 = h₀/k₀ < h₁/k₁ < … < h_M/k_M = 1/1 be the Farey sequence F_N. The Rademacher path P(N) is the piecewise-C¹ path in the upper half-plane from i to 1 + i obtained by concatenating: the arc of C(0, 1) from i to the tangency point α₂(0, 1) with C(h₁, k₁), lying in Re τ ≥ 0; for 1 ≤ j ≤ M − 1 the arc of C(h_j, k_j) from α₁(h_j, k_j) to α₂(h_j, k_j) not containing h_j/k_j (the upper arc); and the arc of C(1, 1) from α₁(1, 1) to 1 + i, lying in Re τ ≤ 1. Consecutive arcs share their endpoints, and the path meets the real axis nowhere. After translating the first arc by 1, P(N) is the union over h/k ∈ F_N ∖ {0} of the upper arcs Ũ_{h,k} of C(h, k) between its tangency points with the neighbours of h/k in the periodically extended F_N.
hypotheses: N ≥ 1; the path is given as a function [0, M + 1] → ℂ that is C¹ on each [j, j + 1], in Tau Ceti's `IsPiecewiseC1On` sense.
proofSteps: Consecutive Farey fractions satisfy bc − ad = 1 (ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.2/farey-neighbour-property), so consecutive Ford circles are tangent (ford-circles-tangent-or-disjoint) at α₂(h_j, k_j) = α₁(h_{j+1}, k_{j+1}) (ford-circle-tangency-point).
Parametrise each arc by angle about the centre of its circle; the pieces are C¹ and agree at the tangency points.
Points of C(h, k) other than h/k have positive imaginary part (fordCircle API), and the upper arcs avoid h/k.
Translation invariance C(q + 1) = C(q) + 1 identifies the arc of C(0, 1) translated by 1 with the continuation of the arc of C(1, 1).
acceptance: P(1) is the arc of C(0, 1) from i to (1 + i)/2 followed by the arc of C(1, 1) from (1 + i)/2 to 1 + i.
P(2) passes through the tangency points 2/5 + i/5 and 3/5 + i/5 of C(1, 2) with C(0, 1) and C(1, 1).

nodes.title: The Laplace transform of a complex power
nodes.statement: For s, t ∈ ℂ with Re s > 0 and Re t > 0: ∫_{(0,∞)} u^{s−1} e^{−tu} du = Γ(s) · t^{−s}, with Mathlib's principal complex power (arg t ∈ (−π/2, π/2)).
hypotheses: Re s > 0 (integrability at 0) and Re t > 0 (integrability at ∞).
proofSteps: For real t = r > 0 this is `Complex.integral_cpow_mul_exp_neg_mul_Ioi` ((1/r)^s Γ(s) = r^{−s} Γ(s)).

Both sides are holomorphic in t on the open half-plane {Re t > 0}: the left side by differentiation under the integral (`hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le`, dominated on Re t ≥ δ by u^{Re s} e^{−δu}), the right side as t^{−s} on the slit plane.

The half-plane is convex, hence preconnected (`Convex.isPreconnected`), and the two sides agree on the real ray, which accumulates at t = 1; conclude by `AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_of_preconnected_of_frequently_eq` (with `DifferentiableOn.analyticOnNhd`).

nodes.title: Laplace's integral for the reciprocal of the Gamma function
nodes.statement: For every real c > 0 and every s ∈ ℂ with Re s > 1: 1/Γ(s) = (1/(2π)) ∫_{−∞}^{∞} (c + iy)^{−s} e^{c + iy} dy, i.e. 1/Γ(s) = (1/(2πi)) ∫_{c−i∞}^{c+i∞} t^{−s} e^{t} dt, the integral converging absolutely; t^{−s} is the principal power.
hypotheses: c > 0; Re s > 1 (absolute convergence on the vertical line).
proofSteps: Let g(u) = u^{s−1} e^{−cu}/Γ(s) for u > 0 and g(u) = 0 for u ≤ 0. Then g ∈ L¹(ℝ) and g is continuous at u = 1.
Its Fourier transform, in Mathlib's normalisation 𝓕g(ξ) = ∫ e^{−2πiuξ} g(u) du, is (c + 2πiξ)^{−s} by laplace-transform-cpow with t = c + 2πiξ.
|(c + 2πiξ)^{−s}| ≤ e^{π|Im s|/2} |c + 2πiξ|^{−Re s} is integrable because Re s > 1.
Fourier inversion at u = 1 (`MeasureTheory.Integrable.fourierInv_fourier_eq`): e^{−c}/Γ(s) = ∫ (c + 2πiξ)^{−s} e^{2πiξ} dξ; substitute y = 2πξ and multiply by e^{c}.

The value does not depend on c > 0.

nodes.title: The modified Bessel function of the first kind
nodes.statement: For ν, z ∈ ℂ, I_ν(z) = (z/2)^ν Σ_{j≥0} (z²/4)^j / (j! Γ(ν + j + 1)), where (z/2)^ν is Mathlib's principal complex power and 1/Γ is entire, so every coefficient is defined. Equivalently I_ν(z) = (z/2)^ν · Complex.regularizedHGFun 0 {ν + 1} (z²/4), Mathlib's regularized ₀F̃₁. The series has infinite radius of convergence; I_ν is holomorphic on the slit plane ℂ ∖ (−∞, 0] and entire for ν ∈ ℤ; for real ν > −1 and real x > 0, I_ν(x) is real and positive. At z = 0 Mathlib's convention 0^ν = 0 (ν ≠ 0) and 0^0 = 1 applies, so I_0(0) = 1 and I_ν(0) = 0 for ν ≠ 0.
hypotheses: ν ∈ ℂ arbitrary; statements on the slit plane use the principal branch of (z/2)^ν.
proofSteps: Define the function through `Complex.regularizedHGFun` with a = 0, b = {ν + 1}: its coefficients are 1/(j! Γ(ν + 1 + j)) (`Complex.regularizedHGFunCoeff`).
Infinite radius: `Complex.radius_regularizedHGFunSeries_eq_top` (card a = 0 ≤ card b = 1), so z ↦ ₀F̃₁(; ν + 1; z²/4) is entire.
Positivity for ν > −1, x > 0: every term (x/2)^{ν+2j}/(j! Γ(ν + j + 1)) is positive since Γ > 0 on (0, ∞).

nodes.title: The vertical-line integral for I_ν
nodes.statement: For real x > 0, real c > 0 and ν ∈ ℂ with Re ν > 0: I_ν(x) = (x/2)^ν · (1/(2π)) ∫_{−∞}^{∞} (c + iy)^{−ν−1} exp(c + iy + x²/(4(c + iy))) dy, i.e. I_ν(x) = (x/2)^ν (1/(2πi)) ∫_{c−i∞}^{c+i∞} t^{−ν−1} exp(t + x²/(4t)) dt, the integral converging absolutely.
hypotheses: x > 0, c > 0, Re ν > 0. The source states the formula for every complex ν; for Re ν ≤ −1 the integral diverges (QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms/E302).
proofSteps: Expand exp(x²/(4t)) = Σ_j (x²/4)^j t^{−j}/j!.
On Re t = c: |t^{−ν−1−j}| ≤ e^{π|Im ν|/2} |t|^{−Re ν−1} c^{−j} and |e^t| = e^c, so Σ_j ∫ |term| dy ≤ e^{c + π|Im ν|/2 + x²/(4c)} ∫ |c + iy|^{−Re ν−1} dy < ∞ since Re ν > 0; exchange sum and integral.
Each term: (1/(2π)) ∫ (c + iy)^{−(ν+1+j)} e^{c+iy} dy = 1/Γ(ν + j + 1) by bromwich-integral-reciprocal-gamma (Re(ν + 1 + j) > 1).

nodes.title: The Kloosterman sum A_k(n) of the Rademacher series
nodes.statement: For k ≥ 1 and n ∈ ℤ, A_k(n) = Σ_{0 ≤ h < k, gcd(h, k) = 1} exp(πi·s(h, k) − 2πinh/k), where s(h, k) = Σ_{r=1}^{k−1} (r/k)((hr/k)) is the Dedekind sum of QM.1 (((x)) = x − ⌊x⌋ − 1/2 for x ∉ ℤ and ((x)) = 0 for x ∈ ℤ; s(h, 1) = 0), so ω_{h,k} = exp(πi s(h, k)) is the 24k-th root of unity of the eta multiplier at (H, −K; k, −h). A_k(n) is real, depends only on n mod k, and |A_k(n)| ≤ φ(k).
hypotheses: k ≥ 1; the summation runs over a reduced residue system mod k, and s(h, k) depends only on h mod k.
proofSteps: Define the finite sum over h ∈ Finset.range k with Nat.Coprime h k.
Periodicity in n: e^{−2πi(n+k)h/k} = e^{−2πinh/k}.
Reality: h ↦ k − h permutes the reduced residues and s(k − h, k) = −s(h, k) (oddness of the Dedekind sum, QM.1), so the terms at h and k − h are complex conjugate.
|A_k(n)| ≤ φ(k): triangle inequality, each term of modulus 1.

nodes.title: The Jacobi-symbol form of the roots of unity ω_{h,k}
nodes.statement: Let k ≥ 1 and gcd(h, k) = 1, and let h̄ ∈ ℤ with hh̄ ≡ 1 (mod k). Then exp(πi s(h, k)) equals (−h | k) · exp(−πi[(k − 1)/4 + (1/12)(k − 1/k)(2h + h̄ − h²h̄)]) if k is odd, and (−k | h) · exp(−πi[(2 − hk − h)/4 + (1/12)(k − 1/k)(2h + h̄ − h²h̄)]) if k is even (so h is odd), where (a | b) is the Jacobi symbol (Mathlib's `jacobiSym`). Consequently A_k(n) = Σ_h ω^J_{h,k} e^{−2πinh/k} with these roots of unity, the definition used by Hardy–Ramanujan, Lehmer and Whiteman.
hypotheses: The right sides do not depend on the choice of h̄ modulo k.
Hardy–Ramanujan write the same numbers with p′ = −h̄ (1 + pp′ ≡ 0 mod q).
proofSteps: Both sides are 24k-th roots of unity; the identity is equivalent to the congruence 12k·s(h, k) ≡ 12k·(right-hand exponent) modulo 24k, which splits by the Chinese remainder theorem into congruences modulo 8, modulo 3 and modulo k (or 3k).
Modulo k (or θk with θ = gcd(3, k)): 12hk·s(h, k) ≡ h² + 1, from the definition of s(h, k) by summing the sawtooth.

Modulo 8 for k odd: 12k·s(h, k) ≡ k + 1 − 2(h | k), by induction along the Euclidean algorithm using Dedekind reciprocity (QM.1) and Jacobi reciprocity (`jacobiSym.quadratic_reciprocity`); the even-k case follows from the reciprocity law.
These steps have no public source read for this layer; see the gap 'Jacobi-symbol closed form of the eta multiplier'.
acceptance: Checked numerically for every k ≤ 40 and every h coprime to k (agreement of both sides to 10⁻²⁰).

nodes.title: Lehmer's exponent form of A_k(n)
nodes.statement: For k ≥ 1 and n ∈ ℤ, A_k(n) = Σ_ρ exp(πi f_n(ρ, k)/(12k)) if k is odd and A_k(n) = Σ_ρ exp(πi g_n(ρ, k)/(12k)) if k is even, where ρ runs over a reduced residue system modulo k, ρ̄ ∈ ℤ with ρρ̄ ≡ 1 (mod k), and f_n(ρ, k) = −{24nρ + 6k(−ρ | k) + 3k(k − 3) + (k² − 1)(2ρ + ρ̄ − ρ²ρ̄)}, g_n(ρ, k) = −{24nρ + 6k(−k | ρ) − ρ(k + 1)(k + 2) − (k² − 1)(ρ² − 1)ρ̄}. The summands depend only on ρ mod k (f_n, g_n are well defined modulo 24k).
hypotheses: k ≥ 1; for k even the representatives ρ are odd.
proofSteps: Substitute (a | b) = exp[(1 − (a | b))πi/2] (valid since (a | b) = ±1) in the Jacobi-symbol form of node kloosterman-sum-rademacher-jacobi-form and collect the exponent over the common denominator 12k.
Independence of representatives: replacing ρ̄ by ρ̄ + k changes f_n by (k² − 1)(1 − ρ²)k, a multiple of 24k (k² − 1 ≡ 0 mod 8, and 3 | (k² − 1)(1 − ρ²)).
acceptance: Checked numerically for 1 ≤ k < 50 and 0 ≤ n ≤ 5.

nodes.title: Lehmer's fundamental congruences
nodes.statement: Let ν = 1 − 24n. In each congruence ρ̄ denotes an inverse of ρ modulo the modulus of that congruence. If k is odd: f_n(ρ) ≡ νρ + ρ̄ (mod k, or mod 3k when 3 | k); f_n(ρ) ≡ 0 (mod 3) when 3 ∤ k; f_n(ρ) ≡ 2k(−ρ | k) + k − 3 (mod 8). If k = 2^λ k₁ with k₁ odd and λ ≥ 1: g_n(ρ) ≡ νρ + ρ̄ (mod k₁, or mod 3k₁ when 3 | k₁); g_n(ρ) ≡ 0 (mod 3) when 3 ∤ k₁; g_n(ρ) ≡ νρ + ρ̄ + 2k(−k | ρ) + k(k + 3)ρ (mod 2^{λ+3}).
hypotheses: f_n = f_n(·, k) and g_n = g_n(·, k) as in node lehmer-exponent-form.
proofSteps: Reduce the defining polynomials: modulo k, (k² − 1) ≡ −1 and ρρ̄ ≡ 1 give f_n ≡ −24nρ + ρ + ρ̄; modulo 3k when 3 | k, use k² − 1 ≡ −1 (mod 3k) likewise.
Modulo 3 when 3 ∤ k: 24nρ ≡ 0, k² − 1 ≡ 0, and 6k(·) + 3k(k − 3) ≡ 0.
Modulo 8 for k odd: 24nρ ≡ 0 and k² − 1 ≡ 0, −6k ≡ 2k and −3k(k − 3) ≡ k − 3 (mod 8, using k² ≡ 1); the even case modulo 2^{λ+3} is the same reduction applied to g_n.
acceptance: Checked numerically for 1 ≤ k < 60, 0 ≤ n ≤ 4 and every reduced residue ρ.

nodes.title: Lehmer's multiplication theorem for odd coprime moduli
nodes.statement: Let k₁, k₂ be odd, coprime and positive, and n₁, n₂ ∈ ℤ. Then A_{k₁}(n₁) A_{k₂}(n₂) = A_{k₁k₂}(n₃) for every n₃ ∈ ℤ with n₃ ≡ k₁²n₂ + k₂²n₁ − (k₁² + k₂² − 1)/24 (mod k₁k₂), where the fraction is read modulo k₁k₂: its numerator is ≡ 1 (mod 24) when 3 ∤ k₁k₂ and the fraction has the form M/8 otherwise, and 24 (resp. 8) is inverted modulo k₁k₂.
hypotheses: k₁, k₂ odd, positive and coprime. A_k(n) depends only on n mod k, so n₃ is well defined modulo k₁k₂.
proofSteps: Write both factors by the exponent form (lehmer-exponent-form) and pair the summation indices by ρ₃ ≡ ρ₁/k₂ (mod k₁), ρ₃ ≡ ρ₂/k₁ (mod k₂) (Chinese remainder theorem): ρ₃ runs over the reduced residues modulo k₁k₂.

Show D₁ = f_{n₃}(ρ₃, k₁k₂) − {k₂ f_{n₁}(ρ₁, k₁) + k₁ f_{n₂}(ρ₂, k₂)} ≡ 0 (mod 24k₁k₂): modulo 3 and modulo k₁ (or 3k₁) by the first two congruences of lehmer-exponent-congruences, and modulo 8 by the third together with the multiplicativity of the Jacobi symbol, splitting the cases k₁ ≡ k₂ ≡ 3 (mod 4) and the others.
acceptance: Checked numerically for all odd coprime k₁, k₂ ≤ 15 with k₁k₂ ≤ 120 and all residues n₁, n₂.

nodes.statement: Let k ≥ 1 be odd and λ ≥ 2. Then A_k(n₁) A_{2^λ}(n₂) = (−1)^{2^{λ−2}} A_{2^λ k}(n₃) for every n₃ with n₃ ≡ k²n₂ + 2^{2λ}n₁ − (k² − 1 + 2^{2λ})/24 (mod 2^λ k), the fraction read modulo 2^λ k (its numerator is divisible by 8, and 3 is inverted when 3 ∤ k).

nodes.title: The terms R_k(n) of the Rademacher series
nodes.statement: For k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 1 put λ_n = √(n − 1/24), α(n) = π√(2/3)·λ_n = (π/6)√(24n − 1) and u = α(n)/k. The k-th Rademacher term is the real number R_k(n) = A_k(n)·√k·(u cosh u − sinh u)/(2√2·π·λ_n³), where A_k(n) (real by kloosterman-sum-rademacher) is Rademacher's Kloosterman sum. Equivalently R_k(n) = (1/(π√2)) A_k(n) √k · d/dm [sinh((π/k)√((2/3)(m − 1/24)))/√(m − 1/24)] at m = n, and R_k(n) = (2π/(24n − 1)^{3/4}) · (A_k(n)/k) · I_{3/2}(π√(24n − 1)/(6k)).
hypotheses: k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 1 (so n − 1/24 > 0); the derivative form differentiates in a real variable m near n.
proofSteps: Definition by the elementary closed form.
Derivative form: d/dm = (1/(2λ)) d/dλ and d/dλ[sinh(Cλ/k)/λ] = ((Cλ/k) cosh(Cλ/k) − sinh(Cλ/k))/λ² with C = π√(2/3).

Bessel form: modified-bessel-i-three-halves gives I_{3/2}(x) = √(2/(πx))·(x cosh x − sinh x)/x; with x = α(n)/k, 24n − 1 = 24λ_n² and α(n) = π√(2/3)λ_n one checks (2π/(24n − 1)^{3/4})·(1/k)·√(2/(πx))·(1/x) = √k/(2√2πλ_n³).

nodes.title: p(n) as a path integral in the upper half-plane
nodes.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ. For every τ₀ in the upper half-plane and every piecewise-C¹ path γ in the upper half-plane from τ₀ to τ₀ + 1, p(n) = ∫_γ F(e^{2πiτ}) e^{−2πinτ} dτ. In particular p(n) = ∫_{P(N)} F(e^{2πiτ}) e^{−2πinτ} dτ for the Rademacher path P(N), N ≥ 1.
hypotheses: γ piecewise C¹ (Tau Ceti `IsPiecewiseC1On`), with values in {Im τ > 0}, γ(a) = τ₀, γ(b) = τ₀ + 1.
proofSteps: On the horizontal segment σ from τ₀ to τ₀ + 1 the series Σ_m p(m) e^{2πi(m − n)τ} converges uniformly (|e^{2πiτ}| = e^{−2π Im τ₀} < 1, hasSum_partitionGenFun); integrating termwise, only m = n contributes, so ∫_σ = p(n).
The integrand τ ↦ F(e^{2πiτ})e^{−2πinτ} is holomorphic on the open convex set {Im τ > 0} (`UpperHalfPlane.isOpen_upperHalfPlaneSet`, `convex_halfSpace_im_gt`).

The concatenation of γ with the reversed segment σ is a closed piecewise-C¹ curve in {Im τ > 0}; Cauchy's theorem on a star-shaped open set (`TauCeti.Contour.cauchyTheorem_starConvex`) gives ∫_γ = ∫_σ.
P(N) is such a path from i to 1 + i (rademacher-path).
acceptance: γ = σ itself gives the Fourier-coefficient formula p(n) = ∫_0^1 F(e^{2πi(x+iy)}) e^{−2πin(x+iy)} dx for every y > 0.

nodes.title: Decomposition of the circle-method integral over the Ford arcs
nodes.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, N ≥ 1 and write G = F − 1 and Φ_{n,k}(z) = z^{1/2} exp(π/(12z) + 2π(n − 1/24)z/k²) (principal branch, Re z > 0). For h/k ∈ F_N ∖ {0} with neighbours h₁/k₁ < h/k < h₂/k₂ in the periodically extended F_N, let V_{h,k} be the arc of K = {|z − 1/2| = 1/2} from w₁(h, k) to w₂(h, k) not containing 0 (clockwise), and let H ∈ ℤ with hH ≡ −1 (mod k). Then p(n) = Σ_{k=1}^{N} Σ_h (I_{h,k} + J_{h,k}), h running over the reduced residues modulo k, where I_{h,k} = i·k^{−5/2}·e^{πi s(h,k) − 2πinh/k} ∫_{V_{h,k}} Φ_{n,k}(z) dz and J_{h,k} = i·k^{−5/2}·e^{πi s(h,k) − 2πinh/k} ∫_{V_{h,k}} Φ_{n,k}(z) G(exp(2πiH/k − 2π/z)) dz.
hypotheses: n ∈ ℕ, N ≥ 1; the pairs (h, k) with 1 ≤ h ≤ k ≤ N, gcd(h, k) = 1 are exactly the nonzero terms of F_N.
proofSteps: Split ∫_{P(N)} (partition-number-path-integral) into the arcs Ũ_{h,k} (rademacher-path), moving the first arc to the last by the 1-periodicity of τ ↦ F(e^{2πiτ})e^{−2πinτ}.
On Ũ_{h,k} substitute τ = h/k + iz/k² (ford-circle-local-coordinate): dτ = (i/k²)dz, the arc becomes V_{h,k}, and e^{−2πinτ} = e^{−2πinh/k}e^{2πnz/k²}.
Apply partition-generating-function-transformation and write F = 1 + G; the factor exp(−πz/(12k²)) combines with e^{2πnz/k²} to exp(2π(n − 1/24)z/k²).
The terms of F_N ∖ {0} are the fractions h/k with 1 ≤ h ≤ k ≤ N coprime (ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.2/farey-sequence).
acceptance: N = 1: two arcs merge into the single arc of C(1, 1) = C(0, 1) + 1, and p(n) = I_{0,1} + J_{0,1}.

nodes.statement: For n ∈ ℕ and N ≥ 1, with J_{h,k} as in rademacher-arc-decomposition: |Σ_{k=1}^{N} Σ_h J_{h,k}| ≤ C₁(n)/√(N + 1), where C₁(n) = 2^{7/4}(F(e^{−π/48}) − 1)e^{2πn}.
proofSteps: The integrand of J_{h,k} is holomorphic on the open convex half-plane {Re z > 0} (`convex_halfSpace_re_gt`, `Complex.isOpen_re_gt`): |exp(2πiH/k − 2π/z)| = e^{−2π Re(1/z)} < 1 there, and V_{h,k} and the chord W_{h,k} = [w₁, w₂] lie in it (rademacher-circle-inversion, ford-chord-estimates). By `TauCeti.Contour.cauchyTheorem_starConvex`, ∫_{V_{h,k}} = ∫_{W_{h,k}}.
The chord has length ≤ 2√2k/(N + 1) (ford-chord-estimates), so |J_{h,k}| ≤ 2^{7/4}(F(e^{−π/48}) − 1)e^{2πn}k^{−1}(N + 1)^{−3/2}.
At most k residues h for each k ≤ N: the sum is ≤ C₁(n)·N(N + 1)^{−3/2} ≤ C₁(n)/√(N + 1).
acceptance: The bound tends to 0 as N → ∞ for fixed n; it does not depend on the individual arcs.

nodes.title: Completing the main integrals to the full circle
nodes.statement: For n ∈ ℕ and N ≥ 1, with I_{h,k} as in rademacher-arc-decomposition, put I⁰_{h,k} = −i·k^{−5/2}·e^{πi s(h,k) − 2πinh/k} ∮_K Φ_{n,k}(z) dz, K positively oriented and Φ_{n,k} extended by 0 at z = 0 (continuous on K since |Φ_{n,k}(z)| ≤ |z|^{1/2}e^{π/12 + 2πn} there). Then |Σ_{k=1}^{N} Σ_h (I_{h,k} − I⁰_{h,k})| ≤ C₂(n)/√(N + 1), where C₂(n) = 2^{3/4}π·e^{π/12 + 2πn}.
proofSteps: The clockwise arc V_{h,k} equals the clockwise full circle −K minus the minor arcs W₁ from 0 to w₁ (clockwise) and W₂ from 0 to w₂ (anticlockwise); hence I_{h,k} − I⁰_{h,k} is the sum of two minor-arc integrals.

On W₁ ∪ W₂: |z| ≤ max(|w₁|, |w₂|) ≤ √2k/(N + 1) (rademacher-circle-minor-arc-estimates, ford-chord-estimates) and Re(1/z) = 1 (rademacher-circle-inversion), so |Φ_{n,k}(z)| ≤ 2^{1/4}k^{1/2}(N + 1)^{−1/2}e^{π/12 + 2πn}.
Each minor arc has length ≤ (π/2)·√2k/(N + 1); so |I_{h,k} − I⁰_{h,k}| ≤ 2^{3/4}πe^{π/12 + 2πn}k^{−1}(N + 1)^{−3/2}; sum over ≤ k residues h and k ≤ N.

nodes.title: An elementary bound for u cosh u − sinh u
nodes.statement: For every real u > 0: 0 < u cosh u − sinh u ≤ u³ cosh u / 2.
proofSteps: Positivity: u cosh u − sinh u = Σ_{j≥1} 2j u^{2j+1}/(2j + 1)! > 0.
Cauchy's mean value theorem (`exists_ratio_hasDerivAt_eq_ratio_slope`) for g(u) = u cosh u − sinh u and h(u) = u² on [0, u]: (u cosh u − sinh u)/u² = g′(v)/h′(v) = sinh v/2 for some v ∈ (0, u).
By the mean value theorem sinh v = v cosh w for some w ∈ (0, v), and cosh is increasing on [0, ∞): sinh v ≤ v cosh v ≤ u cosh u.

hypotheses: a > 0 fixed; the O-constant depends on a.
proofSteps: For n ≥ 4/a², N = ⌊a√n⌋ satisfies N ≥ a√n/2 ≥ 1 and N + 1 > a√n.
First term of hardy-ramanujan-truncation-bound: α(n)/(N + 1) < π√(2/3)λ_n/(a√n) ≤ π√(2/3)/a, so it is ≤ (π²/(3√3))√2·a^{−1/2}cosh(π√(2/3)/a)·n^{−1/4}.
acceptance: n = 100, a = 0.6 (N = 6): error 0.004; n = 200, N = 8: error +0.024 (Hardy–Ramanujan print −0.004 there; see QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms/E307).

nodes.title: Wirtinger derivatives ∂/∂τ and ∂/∂τ̄
nodes.statement: For F : ℂ → ℂ and z ∈ ℂ put ∂F(z) := ½(DF(z)(1) − i·DF(z)(i)) and ∂̄F(z) := ½(DF(z)(1) + i·DF(z)(i)), where DF(z) = fderiv ℝ F z is the real Fréchet derivative (junk value 0 where F is not real-differentiable). In coordinates z = u + iv these are ½(∂_u − i∂_v) and ½(∂_u + i∂_v). A function f : ℍ → ℂ is differentiated through F = f ∘ ofComplex (which agrees with f on the open set {Im z > 0}); we write ∂_τ f and ∂_τ̄ f for these, following the notation ∂/∂τ, ∂/∂τ̄ of Bruinier–Funke §3.
hypotheses: Two declarations defined together: Complex.wirtingerDeriv (∂) and Complex.wirtingerDerivBar (∂̄); the ℍ-versions are the compositions with UpperHalfPlane.ofComplex, not new definitions.
No holomorphy is assumed; for complex-differentiable F one has ∂F = F′ and ∂̄F = 0.
proofSteps: Define both as ℂ-combinations of fderiv ℝ F z applied to 1 and to i.

Cauchy–Riemann: DF(z) is ℂ-linear iff DF(z)(i) = i·DF(z)(1) iff ∂̄F(z) = 0; then ∂F(z) = DF(z)(1) = deriv F z (Mathlib's HasFDerivAt.restrictScalars direction and the converse by constructing the ℂ-linear map).
Leibniz and conjugation rules: fderiv ℝ of a product and of conj ∘ F, then collect terms.

Laplacian compatibility: expand ∂∂̄ = ¼(∂_u² + ∂_v²) and compare with InnerProductSpace.laplacian_eq_iteratedFDeriv_complexPlane (iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 F z ![1,1] + ![I,I]) for C² functions (symmetry of second derivatives).
acceptance: 4∂∂̄F equals Mathlib's Laplacian of F for every C² function F : ℂ → ℂ.

sources.excerpt: They are deﬁned as the diﬀerential operators R_k = 2i ∂/∂τ + kv^{−1} and L_k = −2iv² ∂/∂τ̄.
sources.match: The operators ∂/∂τ, ∂/∂τ̄ used by the source are exactly these Wirtinger derivatives; the source takes them as standard.
Confirms ∂/∂z̄ = ½(∂/∂x + i∂/∂y), the convention pinned here.

nodes.title: The weight-k hyperbolic Laplacian Δ_k
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℝ and f : ℍ → ℂ, Δ_k f(τ) := −v²(∂²_u + ∂²_v)f(τ) + ikv(∂_u + i∂_v)f(τ) = −4v²∂_τ∂_τ̄ f(τ) + 2ikv ∂_τ̄ f(τ), where τ = u + iv (Bruinier–Funke (3.1); Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (2.1)). Real weight is admitted so that the same operator serves the integral weights of QM.3 and the weight 1/2 of QM.4. Zwegers' weight-1/2 Casimir operator Ω_{1/2} = −4v²∂_τ∂_τ̄ + iv∂_τ̄ + 3/16 equals Δ_{1/2} + 3/16, so 'eigenfunction of Ω_{1/2} with eigenvalue 3/16' means 'annihilated by Δ_{1/2}'.
hypotheses: k ∈ ℝ; f is differentiated through f ∘ ofComplex; the value is only meaningful where f is C².
Sign convention pinned: the first-order term is +ikv(∂_u + i∂_v) = 2ikv∂_τ̄, so holomorphic functions are annihilated for every k.
proofSteps: Define Δ_k f(τ) := −4 (Im τ)² ∂(∂̄(f ∘ ofComplex))(τ) + 2ik (Im τ) ∂̄(f ∘ ofComplex)(τ).
The coordinate form follows from ∂∂̄ = ¼(∂_u² + ∂_v²) and 2∂̄ = ∂_u + i∂_v (QM.3/wirtinger-derivatives).
Δ_k(v^s) = s(1 − k − s)v^s: ∂̄v^s = (is/2)v^{s−1}, ∂∂̄v^s = ¼s(s−1)v^{s−2}; substitute.
The Casimir identity is the case k = 1/2: 2·(1/2)·i v ∂̄ = iv∂̄.
acceptance: Δ_k(1) = 0 and Δ_k(v^{1−k}) = 0 (the two harmonic functions of the constant Fourier term, BF p. 9).
Δ_0 = −v²·Δ with Mathlib's Laplacian Δ.
Δ_k(τ̄) = 2ikv ≠ 0 for k ≠ 0, so the sign of the first-order term is detected.

nodes.title: The Maass raising operator R_k
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℝ and f : ℍ → ℂ, R_k f(τ) := 2i ∂_τ f(τ) + k v^{−1} f(τ). Writing D := (2πi)^{−1}∂_τ (= q d/dq on holomorphic functions) one has R_k = −4πD + k/v (BOR p. 7).
hypotheses: k ∈ ℝ; f real-differentiable where evaluated.
proofSteps: Define R_k f := 2i·∂(f ∘ ofComplex) + (k / Im τ)·f.
R_k = −4πD + k/v since 2i∂ = 2i·2πi·D = −4πD.

nodes.title: Factorisation of Δ_k through raising and lowering
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℝ and f : ℍ → ℂ of class C²: −Δ_k f = L_{k+2}R_k f + k f = R_{k−2}L_k f (Bruinier–Funke (3.3), Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (2.2)).
hypotheses: f of class C² on ℍ (as f ∘ ofComplex on {Im > 0}).
proofSteps: Symmetry ∂∂̄ = ∂̄∂ on C² functions (Mathlib's symmetry of second derivatives).
acceptance: Applied to f = v^{1−k}: L_k v^{1−k} = (1−k)v^{2−k}, R_{k−2}((1−k)v^{2−k}) = 0 (R_w kills v^{−w}), consistent with Δ_k v^{1−k} = 0.

nodes.title: Raising and lowering shift Δ-eigenvalues
nodes.statement: If f : ℍ → ℂ is of class C³ and Δ_k f = λf, then Δ_{k+2}(R_k f) = (λ + k)R_k f and Δ_{k−2}(L_k f) = (λ − k + 2)L_k f (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (2.3), (2.4)).
hypotheses: k ∈ ℝ, λ ∈ ℂ, f of class C³ (so that R_k f, L_k f are C²).
proofSteps: From QM.3/laplacian-raising-lowering-factorisation at weight k + 2: −Δ_{k+2}R_k f = R_k L_{k+2} R_k f = R_k(−Δ_k f − kf) = −(λ + k)R_k f.
At weight k − 2: −Δ_{k−2}L_k f = L_k R_{k−2} L_k f + (k−2)L_k f = L_k(−Δ_k f) + (k − 2)L_k f = −(λ − k + 2)L_k f.
acceptance: For harmonic f of weight 2 − k (λ = 0) iterating gives Δ_{k−2}R^{k−2}_{2−k}f = (2 − k)R^{k−2}_{2−k}f, the step used in the proof of BOR Theorem 1.1.

nodes.title: The ξ-operator ξ_k (shadow operator)
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℝ and f : ℍ → ℂ, ξ_k f(τ) := 2i v^k \overline{∂_τ̄ f(τ)} = v^{k−2} \overline{L_k f(τ)} = R_{−k}(v^k \overline{f})(τ) (Bruinier–Funke Prop. 3.2; Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (1.1)). It is conjugate-linear, kills exactly the holomorphic functions, and maps weight k to weight 2 − k. For a harmonic Maass form f, ξ_k f is its shadow (up to the convention of complex conjugation of coefficients made explicit in QM.3/xi-fourier-expansion).
hypotheses: k ∈ ℝ; v^k is the real power (Im τ)^k.
ξ_k is ℝ-linear and conjugate-linear over ℂ: ξ_k(cf) = c̄ ξ_k f.
proofSteps: Define ξ_k f(τ) := 2i (Im τ)^k conj(∂̄(f ∘ ofComplex)(τ)).
v^{k−2}\overline{L_k f} = v^{k−2}\overline{−2iv²∂̄f} = 2iv^k\overline{∂̄f}.
R_{−k}(v^k f̄) = 2i∂(v^k f̄) − kv^{k−1}f̄ = 2iv^k\overline{∂̄f} + 2ikv^{k−1}(∂v)f̄ − kv^{k−1}f̄ = 2iv^k\overline{∂̄f} (∂v = −i/2).
acceptance: For n < 0: ξ_k(Γ(1−k, 4π|n|v)e(nτ)) = −(4π|n|)^{1−k}e(|n|τ), the normalisation of Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (1.3).

sources.excerpt: The assignment f(τ) ↦ ξ_k(f)(τ) := v^{k−2}\overline{L_kf(τ)} = R_{−k}v^k\overline{f(τ)} deﬁnes an antilinear mapping ξ_k : H_{k,L} → M^!_{2−k,L^−}. Its kernel is M^!_{k,L} ⊂ H_{k,L}.

nodes.title: ξ_{2−k} ∘ ξ_k = −Δ_k
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℝ and f : ℍ → ℂ of class C²: ξ_{2−k}(ξ_k f) = −Δ_k f.
hypotheses: f of class C² on ℍ.
proofSteps: Put h = L_k f, so ξ_k f = v^{k−2}h̄. Compute L_{2−k}(v^{k−2}h̄) = −2iv²∂̄(v^{k−2}h̄) = (k−2)v^{k−1}h̄ − 2iv^k\overline{∂h} (∂̄v = i/2, ∂̄h̄ = \overline{∂h}).
Conjugating: \overline{L_{2−k}(ξ_k f)} = v^k(2i∂h + (k−2)v^{−1}h) = v^k R_{k−2}h.
ξ_{2−k}(ξ_k f) = v^{−k}\overline{L_{2−k}ξ_k f} = R_{k−2}L_k f = −Δ_k f by QM.3/laplacian-raising-lowering-factorisation.
acceptance: For f = v^{1−k}: ξ_k f = 1 − k (constant), ξ_{2−k}(1 − k) = 0 = −Δ_k v^{1−k}.

sources.match: With ξ_k f = v^{k−2}\overline{L_k f} (Prop. 3.2) this identity gives ξ_{2−k}ξ_k = R_{k−2}L_k = −Δ_k, the form in which BF use it (Prop. 3.2, Thm. 3.7).

nodes.title: ξ_k f is holomorphic iff Δ_k f = 0
nodes.statement: Let U ⊆ ℍ be open, k ∈ ℝ and f of class C² on U. Then ξ_k f is holomorphic on U if and only if Δ_k f = 0 on U. Pointwise: ∂_τ(v^k ∂_τ̄ f) = −¼ v^{k−2} Δ_k f.
hypotheses: f of class C² on the open set U (ξ_k f is then C¹, so holomorphy is ∂̄(ξ_k f) = 0).
proofSteps: ∂̄(ξ_k f) = ∂̄(2iv^k\overline{∂̄f}) = 2i·\overline{∂(v^k∂̄f)} (v real), which vanishes iff ∂(v^k∂̄f) = 0 iff Δ_k f = 0.
Holomorphy of a C¹ function is ∂̄ = 0 (QM.3/wirtinger-derivatives, characterisation API).
acceptance: Δ_k(τ̄) = 2ikv ≠ 0 and ξ_k(τ̄) = 2iv^k is not holomorphic for k ≠ 0, consistent with the lemma.
This replaces the Fourier-coefficient argument of Bruinier–Funke Prop. 3.2 (via Lemma 3.1) by a pointwise identity, so it holds on any open set.

sources.excerpt: Proof. By Lemma 3.1, the function ξ_k(f)(τ) is holomorphic on H. It vanishes if and only if f^− vanishes.

nodes.title: R_k and L_k intertwine the slash actions
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℤ, γ ∈ GL₂(ℝ) with det γ = 1 and f : ℍ → ℂ real-differentiable: R_k(f|_kγ) = (R_k f)|_{k+2}γ and L_k(f|_kγ) = (L_k f)|_{k−2}γ, where |_k is Mathlib's weight-k slash action (f|_kγ)(τ) = (cτ + d)^{−k}f(γτ).
hypotheses: det γ = 1 (for det γ > 0 Mathlib's slash carries the extra factor det(γ)^{k−1}, which changes the statement by a scalar).
proofSteps: Chain rule for ∂, ∂̄ along the holomorphic map τ ↦ γτ: ∂(F∘γ) = (∂F∘γ)·γ′, ∂̄(F∘γ) = (∂̄F∘γ)·\overline{γ′}, γ′(τ) = (cτ+d)^{−2}.
R_k(f|_kγ) − (R_kf)|_{k+2}γ = (cτ+d)^{−k−1}f(γτ)·[−2ikc + (k/v)(cτ+d) − (k/v)(cτ̄+d)] = (cτ+d)^{−k−1}f(γτ)·[−2ikc + (k/v)·c·2iv] = 0, using ∂(cτ+d)^{−k} = −kc(cτ+d)^{−k−1} and 1/Im(γτ) = |cτ+d|²/v.
For L_k only ∂̄ of the holomorphic factor (cτ+d)^{−k} vanishes; v² transforms by |cτ+d|^{−4}, giving weight k − 2.
acceptance: For γ = T (translation) both identities reduce to translation invariance; for γ = S they are the classical S-covariance.

sources.excerpt: With respect to the Petersson slash operator (see (6.2)), these operators satisfy the intertwining properties R_k(f |_k γ) = (R_kf) |_{k+2} γ, L_k(f |_k γ) = (L_kf) |_{k−2} γ, for any γ ∈ SL_2(R).

nodes.title: Δ_k commutes with the weight-k slash action
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℤ, γ ∈ GL₂(ℝ) with det γ = 1 and f of class C² on ℍ: Δ_k(f|_kγ) = (Δ_k f)|_kγ. In particular the Δ_k-harmonic functions of weight k form a space stable under the slash action.
hypotheses: det γ = 1.
proofSteps: −Δ_k = R_{k−2}L_k (QM.3/laplacian-raising-lowering-factorisation).
Apply QM.3/raising-lowering-slash-equivariance twice: R_{k−2}L_k(f|_kγ) = R_{k−2}((L_kf)|_{k−2}γ) = (R_{k−2}L_kf)|_kγ.
acceptance: If f is harmonic of weight k then so is f|_kγ; used for the Maass–Poincaré series (termwise harmonicity).

sources.excerpt: The raising operator R_k maps A_{k,L} to A_{k+2,L}, and the lowering operator L_k maps A_{k,L} to A_{k−2,L}.

nodes.title: ξ_k intertwines weight k and weight 2 − k
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℤ, γ ∈ GL₂(ℝ) with det γ = 1 and f real-differentiable on ℍ: ξ_k(f|_kγ) = (ξ_k f)|_{2−k}γ.
hypotheses: det γ = 1.
proofSteps: ξ_k(f|_kγ)(τ) = 2iv^k\overline{∂̄[(cτ+d)^{−k}f(γτ)]} = 2iv^k(cτ̄+d)^{−k}(cτ+d)^{−2}\overline{(∂̄f)(γτ)} (chain rule, ∂̄ of the holomorphic factor vanishes).
(ξ_kf)|_{2−k}γ(τ) = (cτ+d)^{k−2}·2i(v/|cτ+d|²)^k\overline{(∂̄f)(γτ)} = 2iv^k(cτ+d)^{−2}(cτ̄+d)^{−k}\overline{(∂̄f)(γτ)}; the two agree.
acceptance: If f is Γ-invariant of weight k then ξ_k f is Γ-invariant of weight 2 − k (the transformation half of BF Prop. 3.2).

sources.excerpt: It is meromorphic at the cusp via the growth condition on f . The transformation behavior of ξ_k(f)(τ) is easily checked.

nodes.title: Iterated raising operator R^n_k
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℝ, n ∈ ℕ: R^0_k := id and R^{n+1}_k := R_{k+2n} ∘ R^n_k, so R^n_k = R_{k+2(n−1)} ∘ ⋯ ∘ R_{k+2} ∘ R_k maps weight k to weight k + 2n (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades p. 7). Closed form (Lewis–Zagier (4.15), with ∂_h := D − h/(2πv) = −(4π)^{−1}R_{2h}): R^n_k = (−4π)^n Σ_{m=0}^{n} n!/(n−m)! · binom(n + k − 1, m) · (−1/(4πv))^m D^{n−m}, D = (2πi)^{−1}∂_τ.
hypotheses: k ∈ ℝ, n ∈ ℕ; f of class C^n; binom(x, m) is the generalised binomial coefficient for real x.
proofSteps: Define by recursion on n.
Closed form by induction on n using D(v^{−m}) = m v^{−m−1}/(4π) (Lewis–Zagier's (4.15), rewritten through R_w = −4π(D − w/(4πv))).
acceptance: R^1_k = R_k and R^2_0 e(τ) = (16π² − 8π/v)e(τ).
In the closed form, the specialisation n = k − 1 in weight 2 − k kills all terms with m ≥ 1 (Bol's identity).

sources.excerpt: For any positive integer n we put R^n_k := R_{k+2(n−1)} ◦ · · · ◦ R_{k+2} ◦ R_k. We also let R^0_k be the identity.

nodes.title: Bol's identity D^{k−1} = (−4π)^{1−k}R^{k−1}_{2−k}
nodes.statement: For an integer k ≥ 2 and f : ℍ → ℂ of class C^{k−1}: D^{k−1}f = (−4π)^{1−k} R^{k−1}_{2−k} f, where D = (2πi)^{−1}∂_τ. Consequently, for k ∈ ℤ and det γ = 1, D^{k−1}(f|_{2−k}γ) = (D^{k−1}f)|_kγ.
proofSteps: Specialise QM.3/iterated-raising-operator's closed form to n = k − 1, weight 2 − k: binom(n + (2−k) − 1, m) = binom(0, m) = 0 for m ≥ 1, leaving (−4π)^{k−1}D^{k−1}.
The equivariance follows from iteratedRaising_slash.

nodes.title: The upper incomplete gamma function Γ(s, x)
nodes.statement: For s ∈ ℝ and x > 0, Γ(s, x) := ∫_x^∞ t^{s−1}e^{−t} dt (DLMF 8.2.2); the integral converges for every real s because x > 0. Totalised by Γ(s, x) := 0 for x ≤ 0. For s > 0: Γ(s, x) + γ(s, x) = Γ(s), with Tau Ceti's lower incomplete gamma γ(s, x) = TauCeti.lowerIncompleteGamma s x.
hypotheses: Real parameter s (every real value, including s ≤ 0), real argument x > 0. The complex and branch-cut continuations of DLMF 8.2 are not needed.
proofSteps: Define as the Bochner integral over (x, ∞) of t^{s−1}e^{−t} (integrable: t^{s−1}e^{−t} ≤ C e^{−t/2} on [x, ∞)).
Γ(s,x) + γ(s,x) = Γ(s) for s > 0: split ∫_0^∞ at x (Real.Gamma_eq_integral, TauCeti.lowerIncompleteGamma_eq_integral).
Recurrence Γ(s+1, x) = sΓ(s, x) + x^s e^{−x}: integrate by parts on [x, ∞) (DLMF 8.8.2).
d/dx Γ(s, x) = −x^{s−1}e^{−x} for x > 0 (fundamental theorem of calculus).
Γ(n+1, x) = n! e^{−x}Σ_{j≤n}x^j/j! by the recurrence and Γ(1, x) = e^{−x} (DLMF 8.4.8, 8.4.5).
Γ(1/2, x²) = √π erfc(x) for x > 0: substitute t = u² (DLMF 8.4.6) and compare with TauCeti.Real.erfc.
Γ(s, x) ~ x^{s−1}e^{−x} as x → ∞ (DLMF 8.11.2, first term): l'Hôpital with the derivative formula.
acceptance: The function is defined at s = 0 (Γ(0, x) = E₁(x)), where the complete Gamma function has a pole.

nodes.title: The decaying non-holomorphic Fourier basis functions
nodes.statement: Let w ∈ ℝ, h > 0 and n ∈ ℤ with n < 0, and put φ_n(τ) := Γ(1 − w, 4π|n|v/h)·e(nτ/h). Then Δ_w φ_n = 0, ξ_w φ_n = −(4π|n|/h)^{1−w}·e(|n|τ/h), L_w φ_n(τ) = −v^{2−w}(4π|n|/h)^{1−w}e(nτ̄/h), and φ_n(τ) = O(v^{−w}e^{−2π|n|v/h}) as v → ∞. Also Δ_w(v^{1−w}) = 0 and ξ_w(v^{1−w}) = 1 − w.
hypotheses: w ∈ ℝ arbitrary; n < 0; h > 0 (the cusp width).
proofSteps: Write φ_n = b(v)e(nu/h) with b(v) = Γ(1−w, cv)e^{cv/2}, c = 4π|n|/h; use d/dx Γ(1−w, x) = −x^{−w}e^{−x} (QM.3/upper-incomplete-gamma).

With c = 4π|n|/h one has e(nτ/h) = e^{2πinu/h}e^{cv/2}; since 2πin/h + ic/2 = 0 for n < 0, the terms without a derivative of Γ cancel and ∂̄φ_n = −(i/2)c(cv)^{−w}e^{−cv/2}e^{2πinu/h} = −(i/2)c^{1−w}v^{−w}e(nτ̄/h).
ξ_w φ_n = 2iv^w\overline{∂̄φ_n} = −c^{1−w}e(−nτ/h) = −(4π|n|/h)^{1−w}e(|n|τ/h); holomorphic, hence Δ_w φ_n = 0 by QM.3/xi-holomorphic-iff-harmonic; L_w φ_n = −2iv²∂̄φ_n gives the stated formula.
Growth: Γ(1−w, x) = O(x^{−w}e^{−x}) (QM.3/upper-incomplete-gamma asymptotic) and |e(nτ/h)| = e^{2π|n|v/h}.
acceptance: For h = 1 and w = 2 − k this is the term c^−(n)Γ(k−1, 4π|n|y)q^n of Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (1.2), and the ξ formula is their (1.3).

sources.excerpt: It is immediately checked that e^{−w} is a solution. A second, linearly independent solution is found by reduction of the order. Here we choose the function H(w) = e^{−w} ∫_{−2w}^∞ e^{−t}t^{−k} dt.

nodes.title: The growing non-holomorphic Fourier basis functions
nodes.statement: Let w ∈ ℝ, h > 0, n ∈ ℤ with n > 0, W := 2πnv/h and ψ_n(τ) := e^{−W}(∫_1^W s^{−w}e^{2s}ds)·e(nu/h). Then Δ_w ψ_n = 0 and ξ_w ψ_n = (2πn/h)^{1−w}e(−nτ/h); ψ_n(τ) ~ ½W^{−w}e^{W} as v → ∞. Every solution b of b″ − b + (w/W)(b′ + b) = 0 on W > 0 is a combination of e^{−W} and e^{−W}∫_1^W s^{−w}e^{2s}ds.
hypotheses: n > 0, h > 0, w ∈ ℝ. The base point 1 of the integral is a fixed normalisation; changing it adds a multiple of e^{−W}, i.e. of the holomorphic term e(nτ/h) (see sourceIssue E403).
proofSteps: Reduction of order: b = e^{−W}c turns the ODE into c″ + (w/W − 2)c′ = 0, so c′ = C W^{−w}e^{2W}.
∂̄[b(W)e(nu/h)] = (πin/h)(b + b′)(W) e(nu/h) and b + b′ = W^{−w}e^{W} for b = e^{−W}∫_1^W, so ∂̄ψ_n = (πin/h)W^{−w}e(nτ̄/h).
ξ_w ψ_n = 2iv^w\overline{∂̄ψ_n} = (2πn/h)v^w W^{−w} e(−nτ/h) = (2πn/h)^{1−w}e(−nτ/h); holomorphic, so Δ_w ψ_n = 0 (QM.3/xi-holomorphic-iff-harmonic).
Asymptotics: ∫_1^W s^{−w}e^{2s}ds ~ ½W^{−w}e^{2W} (l'Hôpital).
acceptance: The ξ-image of ψ_n is a negative power of q, so non-zero coefficients of ψ_n in f produce the principal part of ξ_w f.

sources.excerpt: If n ̸= 0, then, writing a(h, n; v) as b(2πnv), it is easily seen that b(w) is a solution of the second order linear diﬀerential equation ∂²b/∂w² − b + (k/w)(∂b/∂w + b) = 0

sources.excerpt: The function H(w) has the asymptotic behavior H(w) ∼ (2|w|)^{−k}e^{−|w|}, for w → −∞, (−2w)^{−k}e^{w}, for w → +∞.

nodes.title: Exponential growth at the cusps
nodes.statement: For c ∈ ℙ¹(ℝ) = OnePoint ℝ, f : ℍ → ℂ and k ∈ ℤ: f has exponential growth at c in weight k if for every g ∈ GL₂(ℝ) with g·∞ = c there is C ∈ ℝ with (f|_kg)(τ) = O(e^{C·Im τ}) as Im τ → ∞ (uniformly in Re τ, i.e. along Mathlib's filter atImInfty). For a subgroup Γ ≤ GL₂(ℝ), f has exponential growth at the cusps of Γ if this holds at every c with IsCusp c Γ. This is condition (ii) of Bruinier–Funke §3 and the growth condition of weakly holomorphic forms; it is the analogue of Mathlib's OnePoint.IsBoundedAt with the bound 1 replaced by e^{C Im τ}.
hypotheses: Two declarations: OnePoint.IsExpGrowthAt c f k (one cusp) and IsExpGrowthAtCusps Γ f k (all cusps of Γ).
proofSteps: Define IsExpGrowthAt c f k :≡ ∀ g : GL₂(ℝ), g • ∞ = c → ∃ C, (f ∣[k] g) =O[atImInfty] (τ ↦ exp(C·Im τ)).
Bounded ⇒ exponential growth (take C = 0), from Mathlib's OnePoint.IsBoundedAt.
Sums: O(e^{C₁v}) + O(e^{C₂v}) = O(e^{max(C₁,C₂)v}); products add weights and constants (slash of products: (f g)|_{k+l}g = (f|_kg)(g|_lg) for det g > 0).
Invariance under g ↦ g·u for upper-triangular u: (f|_k g u)(τ) is a scaled translate of (f|_kg), and exponential growth is preserved (constants change).
acceptance: q^{−1} = e(−τ) has exponential growth at ∞ with C = 2π but is not bounded there.
exp(e(−τ)) does not have exponential growth at ∞ (its modulus is exp(e^{2πv}cos 2πu)).

sources.excerpt: there is a C > 0 such that for any cusp s ∈ Q ∪ {∞} of Γ″ and (δ, φ) ∈ Γ′ with δ∞ = s the function f_s(τ) = φ(τ)^{−2k}ρ^{−1}_L(δ, φ)f(δτ) satisﬁes f_s(τ) = O(e^{Cv}) as v → ∞ (uniformly in u, where τ = u + iv);
sources.match: The scalar case (ρ_L trivial): f|_kδ = O(e^{Cv}) at every cusp. BF allow δ ∈ Γ′; allowing all g ∈ GL₂(ℝ) with g∞ = s is equivalent (upper-triangular change of g).

nodes.title: Weakly holomorphic modular forms M^!_k(Γ)
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ GL₂(ℝ) and k ∈ ℤ, a weakly holomorphic modular form of weight k for Γ is a function f : ℍ → ℂ that is holomorphic on ℍ, satisfies f|_kγ = f for all γ ∈ Γ, and has exponential growth at every cusp of Γ (QM.3/exponential-growth-at-cusps); equivalently (for arithmetic Γ) its expansion at every cusp has only finitely many negative powers of q (QM.3/weakly-holomorphic-laurent-expansion). The ℂ-vector space is M^!_k(Γ). It contains Mathlib's ModularForm Γ k (bounded at the cusps).
hypotheses: Γ : Subgroup (GL (Fin 2) ℝ); theorems about expansions assume Γ arithmetic (Subgroup.IsArithmetic) and, for linearity of the slash action over ℂ, Γ.HasDetOne.
Poles are allowed only at the cusps (the source's 'meromorphic at the cusps'), never in ℍ.
proofSteps: Structure extending SlashInvariantForm Γ k with fields holo' (MDifferentiable) and expGrowth' (IsExpGrowthAtCusps Γ k).
Module structure: pointwise operations; closure uses the API of exponential growth and of slash invariance.
Coercion from ModularForm Γ k: bounded at cusps ⇒ exponential growth (OnePoint.IsBoundedAt.isExpGrowthAt).
Products: M^!_k × M^!_l → M^!_{k+l} (slash of products for det = 1; growth adds).

1/Δ ∈ M^!_{−12}(SL₂(ℤ)): Δ = ModularForm.discriminant never vanishes on ℍ (ModularForm.discriminant_ne_zero), is invariant of weight 12, and e^{−2πv} = O(Δ) at ∞ (ModularForm.exp_isBigO_discriminant), so |1/Δ| = O(e^{2πv}).
Odd weight with −I ∈ Γ: f = f|_k(−I) = (−1)^k f forces f = 0.
acceptance: 1/Δ ∈ M^!_{−12}(SL₂(ℤ)) with expansion q^{−1} + 24 + O(q), not bounded at ∞.
j = E₄³/Δ ∈ M^!_0(SL₂(ℤ)); M_k(Γ) ⊆ M^!_k(Γ).

nodes.title: Laurent expansion of weakly holomorphic forms at a cusp
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ GL₂(ℝ) be arithmetic, f ∈ M^!_k(Γ) and h = Γ.strictWidthInfty > 0. Then there are N ∈ ℕ and a : ℤ → ℂ with a(n) = 0 for n < −N such that f(τ) = Σ_{n∈ℤ} a(n)e(nτ/h), absolutely and locally uniformly convergent on ℍ; a(n) = h^{−1}∫_0^h f(u + iv)e(−n(u+iv)/h)du for every v > 0. Conversely a holomorphic h-periodic function with such an expansion has exponential growth at ∞.
hypotheses: Γ arithmetic, so h > 0 and T^h ∈ Γ (Mathlib's strictPeriods).
proofSteps: f(τ + h) = f(τ) since T^h ∈ Γ; so f(τ) = F(e(τ/h)) with F holomorphic on the punctured unit disc (Mathlib's cuspFunction h f).
|F(q)| = O(|q|^{−C h/2π}) as q → 0 by exponential growth, so F has at most a pole at 0 (Riemann's removable singularity theorem applied to q^N F(q)).
The Laurent expansion of F gives the Fourier expansion; the coefficient formula is the Cauchy integral over |q| = e^{−2πv/h}.

sources.excerpt: We call such modular forms weakly holomorphic. Identity (3.3) implies that M^!_{k,L}(Γ″) ⊂ H_{k,L}(Γ″).
sources.match: Meromorphy at the cusps (the definition used by BF) is the finite Laurent tail proved here from exponential growth.

nodes.title: Harmonic (weak) Maass forms H_k(Γ)
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ GL₂(ℝ) and k ∈ ℤ, a harmonic weak Maass form of weight k for Γ is a function f : ℍ → ℂ of class C² (as f ∘ ofComplex on {Im > 0}) such that (i) f|_kγ = f for all γ ∈ Γ, (ii) f has exponential growth at every cusp of Γ, (iii) Δ_k f = 0. The ℂ-vector space is H_k(Γ) (Bruinier–Funke's H_{k,L}(Γ″) with trivial representation). Choice of setting, pinned: scalar-valued, integral weight k, Γ a subgroup of GL₂(ℝ) (in the theorems: the image of a finite-index subgroup of SL₂(ℤ)); the Weil-representation setting of Bruinier–Funke (vector-valued forms of weight k ∈ ½ℤ for ρ_L on Mp₂(ℤ)) specialises to this one for unimodular L and is not built here. Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades' space 'H_k(Γ₀(N), χ)' is the subspace H_k^+ of QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-plus-space.
hypotheses: k ∈ ℤ; theorems exclude k = 1 where BF do.
C² as in BF; real analyticity (BF: 'automatically real analytic') is not part of the definition and not needed by any result here.
proofSteps: Structure extending SlashInvariantForm Γ k with fields contDiff' (ContDiffOn ℝ 2 (f ∘ ofComplex) on the upper half-plane set), harmonic' (Δ_k f = 0 on ℍ), expGrowth' (IsExpGrowthAtCusps Γ k f).
ℂ-module structure: Δ_k and slash are ℂ-linear (det = 1), growth is closed under sums.
M^!_k(Γ) → H_k(Γ): holomorphic functions are annihilated by Δ_k (hyperbolicLaplacian_of_mdifferentiable) and are C^∞.
Restriction to a subgroup Γ′ ≤ Γ: cusps of Γ′ are cusps of Γ for arithmetic groups (finite index).
acceptance: E₂* = E₂ − 3/(πv) ∈ H_2(SL₂(ℤ)) (QM.3/nonholomorphic-eisenstein-series-e2-star), while E₂ is not: E₂|_2S ≠ E₂.
For odd k and −I ∈ Γ, H_k(Γ) = 0.
